paths.name: Manuel Carlés / Liga Patriótica
paths.notes: Following a bloody struggle, Carlés captures Rosario and assumes the presidency after a rousing speech for his followers in Buenos Aires. Promising vast territorial expansion and an end to the Red Terror that plagues Patagonia, the nationalist rhetoric drummed up by him and his Liga Patriótica Argentina, or Patriotic League of Argentina, is met with a wave of enthusiasm by the struggling people of his country.
objectives: Follow the Liga Patriótica political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.notes:
After a bloody struggle, the Army scores a decisive victory at Rosario, sending forces loyal to Carlés into retreat.

paths.name: Military Coup in Argentina! — Oh no!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Military Coup in Argentina!” becomes available, choose “Oh no!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Continued hesitation to solve the FOP crisis has once again thrown the nation into chaos as military cliques have united to assert control over the nation. Vicious struggles in Buenos Aires, Cordoba and various other cities throughout the nation are still going on but it looks like our government has once again fallen. Fulfilling their promises of strong and direct leadership, the new military government has immediately declared war upon the FOP to once and for all end the crisis.
objectives: When “Military Coup in Argentina!” becomes available, choose “Oh no!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Fall of Buenos Aires — Carlés is dead! Long live Argentina!
paths.shortName: Carlés is dead! Long live Argentina!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Fall of Buenos Aires” becomes available, choose “Carlés is dead! Long live Argentina!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With the majority of the armed supporters of Carlés defeated and captured after the disastrous Rosario campaign, the Army and GOU forces shifted their focus to a quick knock-out of the capital to depose Carlés and re-secure Argentina. Thousands of troops loyal to the Army were sent to the capital where the limited forces of Carlés proved to be no match for their superior counterparts. Last spots of resistance throughout the city still roar but the great leader has already taken his life to avoid capture and punishment for his deeds.

paths.name: The ARA Surrenders to Pedro Pablo Ramírez — En unión y libertad!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The ARA Surrenders to Pedro Pablo Ramírez” becomes available, choose “En unión y libertad!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Unable to continue the fight on their own and with little control over the remainder of the land that was pacified in the early days of the Christmas Coup, Eleazar Videla formally surrendered to the Army at 12 am in the Escuela Superior de Mecánica de la Armada. With the signature of both parties, the internal conflict has effectively ended. Pedro Pablo Ramírez has taken up the task to rebuild the nation and has declared elections to be held in September to decide the future of Argentina.
objectives: When “The ARA Surrenders to Pedro Pablo Ramírez” becomes available, choose “En unión y libertad!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Coup of — Long live President Ramírez!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Coup of” becomes available, choose “Long live President Ramírez!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Unforeseen by Carlés, this morning he was awoken by the marching boots of 8000 Argentine soldiers who had gathered on the Plaza de Mayo. Organised by members of the GOU, General Ramírez took up the lead of the coup, quickly organising their forces to seize key locations in the city before Carlés could react. With the majority of the loyalist soldiers on the borders planning the next offensive, little to no troops were left in the Buenos Aires region leading to a quick and decisive strike on government facilities. Upon arriving at the Navy Petty-Officers School of Mechanics in the neighbourhood of Núñez, the group was attacked by loyal forces who were entrenched there, resulting in the death of 30 and the wounding of 100 but ultimately the surrender of the ARA forces.

Having surrendered the Navy School of Mechanics, the remaining Argentine generals received the rebel leaders and declared Ramírez president of the Republic by noon. Carlés, while able to escape the rebel troops, boarded a small fishing trawler and set off to Peru in the hopes of finding an ally in their regime.
objectives: When “Coup of” becomes available, choose “Long live President Ramírez!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Farrell Takes Over the Office — Long Live President Farrell!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Farrell Takes Over the Office” becomes available, choose “Long Live President Farrell!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Pressured by the members of the now dissolved GOU, Ramírez was forced to resign from office and has allowed Farrell to take office. Farrell has responded by immediately making Peron his vice-president and continuing the social and economic reforms pressed by him. Whether this crack in the military dictatorship will prove to be fatal in the end is yet to be seen but it has proven that stability is yet far from secure.
objectives: When “Farrell Takes Over the Office” becomes available, choose “Long Live President Farrell!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Farrell Refuses to Stand Down — Ramírez resigns.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Farrell Refuses to Stand Down” becomes available, choose “Ramírez resigns.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

In response to Ramirez's demand for his resignation, Farrell has instead tasked the garrison chiefs of Buenos Aires with surrounding the presidential residence and demanding the resignation of Ramirez. Lieutenant-Colonel Tomas Adolfo Duco, convinced that the remaining generals intended to try and launch a coup in support of Ramirez, has called upon the Strategic Infantry Regiment 3 and directed them to the city of Lomas de Zamora, where they have taken key buildings and positions and entrenched themselves in order to pressure Ramirez.
objectives: When “Farrell Refuses to Stand Down” becomes available, choose “Ramírez resigns.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Opposition Falls Apart — Elections are scheduled to occur in two months!
paths.shortName: Elections are scheduled to occur in two months!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Opposition Falls Apart” becomes available, choose “Elections are scheduled to occur in two months!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Just one week later, the nation was shaken up by one of the strangest yet influential events in Argentinian history. An unfamiliar social class, which had remained completely absent from Argentinian history until then, burst into Buenos Aires and demanded Perón's freedom. The city was taken by tens of thousands of workers from the industrial areas that had been growing on the outskirts of the city. The crowd set itself up in the Plaza de Mayo and refused to leave until their demands were met. It was characterised by the large number of young people and especially women who were part of it, and by the predominance of people with hair and skin darker than those who attended the traditional political acts of the time. The anti-Peronist opposition stressed these differences, referring to them in derogatory terms such as "blacks", "fat people", " descamisados (shirtless)", "cabecitas negras". It was the Radical Unionist leader Sammartino who even went so far as to call the event a "zoo flood".

The protestors were accompanied by a whole new generation of young people and new union delegates belonging to the unions of the CGT, which had responded to a sugar workers' strike two days earlier. It was a completely peaceful demonstration, but the political and cultural upheaval was of such heft that, in a few hours, the triumph of the anti-Peronist movement had been cancelled out, as did the remaining power of the military government.

After intense negotiations, the radical Armando Antille distinguished himself as Perón's delegate leading to his liberation. That same night Peron addressed his sympathisers from a balcony at the Casa Rosada and praised their dedication and patriotism.
objectives: When “The Opposition Falls Apart” becomes available, choose “Elections are scheduled to occur in two months!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Elections in the Argentine Republic — Peron becomes president.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Elections in the Argentine Republic” becomes available, choose “Peron becomes president.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

After the massive strikes, protests and the tumultuous incarceration of Peron, election day is finally here. Peron together with his allies in the Unions has organised himself in three new parties to oppose the democratic alliance. Arturo Frondizi, Roberto Ortiz, Ricardo Balbin and Alicia Moreau de Justo have all united against Peron but are still trying to claim the precious presidency for themselves. Small clashes between Peronists and anti-Peronists occurred outside of the voting booths but were quickly suppressed by the police who were tasked with keeping the elections a free process for all.
objectives: When “Elections in the Argentine Republic” becomes available, choose “Peron becomes president.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Death of Manuel Carlés! — We weep for his loss.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Death of Manuel Carlés!” becomes available, choose “We weep for his loss.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

As our Grand Saviour grew older by the day, many inside our government were awaiting the day he finally passed away. Today is this day as the Saviour of Argentina and conqueror of South America has left out his final breath. With no clear successor to secede him and unclarity whether it should be handled within the party or whether elections should be written out, the Council of Buenos Aires has temporarily taken over power. Consisting of many of Carlés' closest associates and the LP inner-party, they will rule the nation with an iron fist until a decision has been made.

Strong pushes by the Peronists have made the elections a close competition between the democratic alliance and the possible presidency of Domingo Peron. Support of the Unions and the rising discontent by the working class has made his popularity skyrocket in recent years, opening up the presidency to his party. Many fear however that Peron's ties to the military would lead to a repeat of the military government and the Ramírez period.

A most interesting facsimile of the New Guangxi Citizen-Militia model has appeared within Europe. In an almost parallel strain of thought, and in a shared desire to be rid of hedonistic selfish values inherent to modern decadent society, theorists within Germany have humoured the concept of programs that mobilise the true potential of a nation's citizeny. Whilst straying from subjugation towards the military akin to the "Wehrstaat", it nonetheless has its uses.

paths.name: The Kuomintang Return to Liangguang — Third time's the charm?
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Kuomintang Return to Liangguang” becomes available, choose “Third time's the charm?”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

In the end, the Kuomintang advance was unstoppable. Despite defeat after defeat, failure after failure, the Kuomintang and its loyalists never gave up. Like Sun Yat-sen before them, the nationalists found a way to return to power in Guangzhou, toppling rival warlords and once more challenging the authority of Beiyang. Thanks to the courageous efforts of General Chen Mingshu and his Tenth Division, marching south from MinGan with the support of leftist elements in the countryside and in the cities, and General Chen Jitang who secured the timely defection of the Guangdong army to the Kuomintang cause, Guangdong has been freed from reactionary oppression. Meanwhile, storming in from their bases in Guizhou, the remnant of the "Seventh Army" the National Revolutionary Army has re-established their control over Guangxi, installing the "New Guangxi clique" under Li Zongren into power.

A provisional revolutionary junta has been established with the three victorious generals representing their respective factions. Calling themselves the South China Political Council, broad ideological and personal divisions remain between the revolutionary generals which are expected to worsen as their supports consolidate political control over their respective regions. It remains to be seen if they will truly be able to live up to their founder's legacy, or if like him their zeal will ultimately fall short of unifying China.
objectives: When “The Kuomintang Return to Liangguang” becomes available, choose “Third time's the charm?”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Federalists Seize Liangguang — All Forward under the Lawyer General!
paths.shortName: All Forward under the Lawyer General!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Federalists Seize Liangguang” becomes available, choose “All Forward under the Lawyer General!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Despite many doubts, the Federalist demise proved to be exaggerated. Chen Jiongming rallied the Guangzhou government's disparate warlord forces, despite the lukewarm support of the city establishment, and overcame Guangxi's warlords and Kuomintang insurgents to restore order to not only his native Guangdong but also Guangxi. For his efforts, he has been rewarded with mastery over the two provinces and a chance to realise his old dream of a Federalist China.

His supporters in Guangdong are ecstatic, even if there are questions about what will happen next. Chen is able to draw support from a broad base that includes his Yue Army loyalists, the gentry and merchant elite, the Guangdong Provincial Assembly, various warlords, and liberal intellectuals. His election to the Governorship, though under dubious circumstances, is now assured as the assembly reconvenes and is expected to extend his term indefinitely.

For Guangxi, the mood is much darker. The Guangdong Army effectively won the war by seizing Nanning and allowing allied warlord bands (many of which were recent defectors) to take other cities as the Old Guangxi Clique collapsed. While all now kowtow to Guangzhou, the prevailing expectation is that Chen will not be able to maintain his hold over Guangxi for long. The sacking of major Guangxi cities by vengeful Guangdong troops and their allies has cast a cloud on their victory.

As Chen works to gather support for a new rival government in southern China, he is expected to confront a dilemma - the same Federalism that won him so much support will prove to be an obstacle for leaving Liangguang for elsewhere.
objectives: When “The Federalists Seize Liangguang” becomes available, choose “All Forward under the Lawyer General!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Old Order Holds in Liangguang — The way things were, but not quite what it ought to be.
paths.shortName: The way things were, but not quite what it ought to be.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

In the end, the revolutionary zeal of the Kuomintang and the republican idealism of the Federalists were insufficient to topple Lu Yuguang and his allies. Rallying their forces, they repelled external invasions by KMT forces and crushed rebellions by socialists, bandits and Cantonese warlords alike. On the surface at least, the old status quo has been restored, with the Young Guangxi Faction remaining dominant in Guangxi, the Shen Army Faction holding onto Shaoguan and northeastern Guangdong, and Chen Lianbo and his Cantonese allies holding onto southern Guangdong.

There is no going back however. The collapse of the old Zhili Order continues to reverberate across China. Even in Liangguang, the power vacuum left behind by the brief period of disorder has shaken the foundations of the post-Northern Expedition system. Power is consolidating away from local, petty warlord factions into the hands of the three remaining strongmen: Lu Yuguang, Shen Hongying, and Chen Lianbo. The latter two are scrambling to secure control over Guangdong, resuming a long-standing battle in the east. The victor may even prove strong enough to challenge Lu Yuguang for all of Liangguang.

For now however, Marshal Lu and the Young Guangxi junta remain in control over the region. They will have to navigate uncertain winds as Liangguang enters the crosshairs of the mighty contenders seeking to unite the nation. Perhaps they will join a side, or perhaps they will create one of their own.

After enduring a tense voyage, Hu Hanmin, the enigmatic leader of the right wing of the Kuomintang, has finally returned to Chinese soil for the first time in a decade. His brilliant mind and towering figure casts a long shadow over the warlord junta, almost immediately dwarfing them in influence.

A devout revolutionary, Hu Hanmin remained largely aloof from the fanfare surrounding his return, greeting the crowds before quickly focusing on more pressing matters. Meeting with various Liangguang power players, including Chen Jitang, Li Zongren, and Chen Mingshu, he has behaved cordially, stating his gratitude for their support whilst keeping thoughts of their crudeness mostly to himself.

Orthodox and studious in approach in interpreting the Three Principles, Hu Hanmin is perhaps the premier expert on the true intentions of his late mentor, Dr. Sun Yat-sen. During his bitter exile, he has formalised his thoughts by writing the "Linkage of the Three Principles", the contents of which seem to have set the groundwork for not only the First Repatriated Congress, but for the Kuomintang movement as a whole.

The start of the party congress has also marked the grand return of the Moscow Committee, and the election of a fourth Central Executive Committee. With 24 members in total, the Central Executive Committee now includes key Moscow figures such as Hu Hanmin, Lin Sen, Ju Zheng, Zou Lu, Li Liejun, Yu Youren, Ding Weifen, Gu Yingfen, Wu Heling, Ye Chucang, Qin Zhen, Shi Qingyang, Shi Ying, Shen Dingyi, Ye Chuqian, and Fu Rulin, alongside more regional figures: Chen Jitang, Lin Yizhong, Li Zongren, and Bai Chongxi.

The Central Supervisory Committee has been constituted by Zhang Ji, Xie Chi, Lin Yungai, and Mao Zuquan.

Notably in absentia is Sun Fo's Reconstruction Faction, corresponding to Sun himself, Wu Chaoshu, and Wang Kunlun in the CEC, and Liang Hancao in the CSC. Serving as an open invitation to the Hawaii Clique, one Hu thoroughly believes Sun can hardly resist, many believe it is a matter of time until he defects to Canton.

Amongst the attendees of the First Conference sits a selection of individuals most disagreeable to the new alignment of our government. The former MinGan officers associated with Chen Mingshu and his old Tenth Division were invited to attend the conference as an expression of unity between the wings of the Kuomintang.

Aligned with the centre-left, Chen and his allies find themselves stuck between a rock and a hard place. Finding few friends and considerable ire within the conference, it is clear that they have been outflanked by Chen Jitang. At the same time, they fear repercussions from their former leftist allies, who have long condemned them for working with the right in any capacity.

Their apparent duplicity has finally caught up with them, with Hu Hanmin being presented with the option to oust them from the conference for their ties to Wang Jingwei. Many of their former rivals in Guangdong like Chen Jitang have pressed the Chairman for their expulsion already charting out plans for an aggressive military campaign and political purge.

Hu however has been more circumspect. An olive branch would weaken Wang's committee and counterbalance his dependence on Chen Jitang, and if successful could further showcase his capability to lead the Revolution. On the other hand, Chen Mingshu is known to be a vehicle for leftist infiltration and tolerating him may have reverberations that follow.

Not all branches of the Revolutionary Party have retained a sense of loyalty towards the derisively named "Moscow Committee" of Hu Hanmin. Most glaringly, the left wing of the party, owing loyalty either to those in the MinGan struggle, or those within Wang Jingwei's Parisian Central Executive Committee. However, the right wing itself is neither united nor whole, considering the emergence of the "New Right" that sprouted from the ideological doctrine of Dai Jitao, one of the Guofu's most close aides and secretaries. Capturing the young and radical members of the party by storm, he has managed to integrate himself with the rather ideologically pragmatic He Yingqin, heir to the late Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and his "Whampoa" Clique of the National Revolutionary Army.

Having occupied Guizhou through force and wit for almost a decade, the Kuomintang within Guizhou are not entirely staffed by those of the New Right, as there are plenty of loyalists that remained faithful to the exiled Central Executive Committee. Chief among them being that of Zhu Peide and his 3rd Army of the NRA, who ruled as the primary figure in the region overseeing his 5-man Junta of the interwar. With Li Zongren and the 7th NRA entering Guangxi, and the subsequent occupation of Guizhou by our forces, there have been many discussions as to the fate of the Rightist Guerrillas.

Proponents of integration of the disparate party insist upon good faith, shows of party unity, and the necessary skillsets provided by the elite of the NRA. Opponents, chief amongst them old rivals of the "New Right" such as those in the Elders, Western Hills, and Reconstruction factions oppose opening the door to those deemed some of the most dangerous to their power within the party's politics.

The last few weeks have marked yet another turning point in Liangguang's tumultuous history. The fallout of the Nanning Mutiny against Guangxi Governor Li Zongren has forced neighbouring Guangdong Governor Chen Mingshu's hand. The General, highly unpopular among the radical left, sent his troops out to restore order in Guangxi, destabilising Guangdong in the process. Sensing the power vacuum, radical Kuomintang and Syndicalist Party unions led by Tan Pingshan called a general strike while peasant militias under Peng Pai uprose, both hoping to secure Chen's removal for their own benefit. Realising the situation, Chen Mingshu hurried home.

The Liangguang narrowly avoided plunging into civil war thanks to Tan Pingshan's rapid victory. Successfully securing major cities and large towns, urban militias and defecting Fourth Army units broke poorly arranged siege attempts by Peng Pai and defended their positions against Chen Mingshu's counterattacks. Within a few days they were in control of all major depots and arsenals in the province.

Seeing where the winds were blowing, both rival armies evaporated almost overnight. Similarly, Wang Jingwei and the Central Committee has seen Tan's victory as fait accompli, recognising him as Governor of Guangdong. With Liang Hancao and Chen Yaozu having fled the province, he is the last man standing of the old standing committee. Zuo Yubai has been named as Guangxi's Governor, but with the province in ruins he is little more than Tan's prefect.

Tan has some friends in high places. Although he has had a tempestuous relationship with Song Qingling and Deng Yanda, who he blames for pushing him out of his own Provisional Action Committee, he is still seen as one of them. Similarly, despite leaving the Chinese Syndicalist Party on largely bad terms, the national branch mostly threw their weight behind him. It is said that even his former co-worker Chen Gongbo interceded for him with Wang Jingwei, so apparently he has not burnt all of all bridges. So, in the end Tan got what he wished - with one telegram Chen Mingshu was dismissed and Tan became Governor.

If there is some lesson about humility to be found here, Tan has not learned it. If anything, this has reinforced his belief that he is the only one who can unite the warring socialist factions. And he has not been subtle about it. Although Chen Mingshu and Peng Pai remain nominally in government, the standing committee has been sidelined and power has been centralised into Tan's hands along with the new Provincial Secretary-General (and Guangdong CSP Party Secretary) Deng Zhongxia. Troops have been deployed into Guangxi, though by the time they arrived the Baise and Longzhou uprisings had proven far more potent than previously thought. Tan has appointed Yu Zuobai as Governor of Guangxi, making it clear who the true master of Liangguang is.

Despite the concerted efforts of the radicals, Guangdong is simply too valuable to the central government to allow it to be destabilised. Wang Jingwei has sent an open statement reminding all that Chen Mingshu as governor and should be afforded the dignity of one. Without naming any names the telegram warns against treasonous behaviour, declaring it contrary to the spirit of party unity. The gambit against Chen has failed.

The message continued with some prattle about the on-going revolution and trust, but few read any further. Chen was victorious and the crisis has made him a household name in Liangguang and beyond, drawing attention to his beliefs and allowing him to present himself as a moderate, benevolent figure in face of growing socialist radicalism.

The Lame General did not hesitate. Although Chen Mingshu and Tan Pingshan remain nominally in government, the standing committee has been sidelined and power has been centralised into Chen's hands along with his chief lieutenant Jiang Guangnai. A detachment has been sent to Guangxi, though by the time they arrived the Baise and Longzhou uprisings had proven far more potent than previously thought. paths.name: A New Mandate for the Old Chairman — A paradox? Or a promise?
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

Quickly, but meticulously, the votes were counted. Hu Hanmin, as expected, has emerged the winner by a slim but still sufficient margin. A short round of celebration emerged spontaneously as the party commemorated its first peaceful, competitive, and relatively fair election, a promising sign for what many hope will come ahead. There were some grumbling of course, especially from those who did not receive sufficient endorsements to make the ballot, but both Ju Zheng and Sun Fo were quick to shake hands and congratulate the winner to quiet any concerns of another party fracture.

Hu Hanmin has taken the stage, congratulating them in turn for an election well run and thanking the party for having faith in him for another term. Waxing poetically, as he usually does, about the philosophical implications of tutelage and his fond memories of Dr. Sun and revolutionaries past, he then turns the discussion to the future. Much work remains ahead, and though Hu's position as the premier party leader is now undisputed, the contradictatory demands placed on him has led many to question his true position on the direction of tutelage. A choice looms, between Hu's utopian dreams that will require the thorough political, social, and economic revolution he has long described and the impossibly speedy rate of progress Hu vows he will complete it in. The party has made its choice today, but what tomorrow holds remains another question.

paths.name: Ju Zheng Wins the Vote — A democracy, but will we have the foundation to keep it?
paths.shortName: A democracy, but will we have the foundation to keep it?
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

Quickly, but meticulously, the votes were counted. A flash of anger struck Hu's face as the results were announced, but he did not lose composure. An arrogant man, but even prouder of his principles, Hu Hanmin accepted his defeat with an icy grace, shaking hands and congratulating the victor before the Congress. In that moment, the transfer of power was complete: Ju Zheng was the new Chairman of the Kuomintang. A short round of celebration emerged spontaneously as the party commemorated its first peaceful, competitive, and relatively fair election, a promising sign for what many hope will come ahead. There were some grumbling of course, especially from those who did not receive sufficient endorsements to make the ballot, but Hu Hanmin's acquiesence and Sun Fo formally conceding the election shortly afterwards sent a clear message: there will be no party fracture.

Ju Zheng has taken the stage, congratulating his opponents on an election well run and thanking the departing Chairman for his long service to the nation. He turns to the audience with the steady, confident voice of a scholar-gentleman. The seed of democracy that the party has sacrificed for all those years has finally sprouted today, and Ju promises to continue to nurture it until it blooms. Quoting Chinese Classics and Sun Yat-sen's teachings with practised poise, his speech reassures the audience of a steady march to the repudiation of the interceding influence of socialism and the foundation of a new Chinese democracy led by gentlemen rather than uncouth warlords or radical rabblerousers. He closes to applause, but some wonder whether or not he is throwing away the party's chance to truly change the nation by moving too quickly.

paths.name: New Guangxi Smashes the Opposition — They shatter like glass.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “New Guangxi Smashes the Opposition” becomes available, choose “They shatter like glass.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Amid the cacophony of discord and several outbreaks of violence among legislators, many doubted whether not elections would even be held. Indeed, plenty had refused to even attend, bowing out thanks to fears of retribution or to spend their hard-earned bribes. A mysterious plague of sudden "illnesses" seemed to afflict key voters ahead of the meeting, but quorum was nevertheless met. Despite the deterioating situation, there was too much on the line for either side's partisans to back down now.

A winner was finally called, but Li Zongren spent little time savour his victory. Dismissing any pleasantries with the now toothless Ju Zheng and the Western Hills clique, he almost immediately brought the weight of New Guangxi to bear against his remaining rivals, gathered neatly in the Yue government to be eliminated together. As New Guangxi aligned propagandists hammered Hu Hanmin, Sun Fo, Chen Jitang, Gu Yingfen, and others who dared to stand up against China's conquering hero. Bai Chongxi and the general staff began drafting up battle plans but it ultimately was for nothing.

Before marching orders could be disseminated, the Yue government dissolved almost overnight. Thanks to a mixture of careful bribes and general demoralisation, most of the elite Guangdong Air Force (perhaps the best paid and most prized arm of the New Guangdong clique) defected to the central government and they were soon joined by an exodus of army defectors. Long wracked by infighting, the warring factions of the Yue government were too divided to even formally dissolve their administration, individually leaving for exile without resigning their posts. Only Hu Hanmin bothered stay in Guangzhou, his second chance at power in shambles.

The central army mops up any remaining resistance and the secret police arrests any one who dares continue to speak out, but all know that Li has already won - even if they are shocked he did so largely without firing a shot. A Kuomintang civil war has been avoided and Li's once shaky position is now secure from within. Now all that remains to be seen is what outsiders have to say about it.

A winner was finally called, but Li Zongren had little time to savour his victory. Almost immediately, it was panned as illegitimate by many leading members of Gui government. Ju Zheng refused to acknowledge his defeat, and the accompanying public protests were much larger than expected, say nothing about the amassing forces under Hu Hanmin's banner. A war between Yue and Gui seemed inevitable, until it was not.

Li Zongren was the first to be arrested. Striding towards his headquarters in his new Presidential outfit, he entered his war room and was consequently ambushed by a special action team. The grim faces of his staff and the presence of Yue-aligned Marshal Li Liejun indicated he would not be President for long. Liejun read out the charges filed against him, but Li refused to go down without a fight. An experienced soldier and a student of martial arts, it took several men to restrain General Li. He roared with rage at the betrayal as his lieutenants stared emotionlessly, but Marshal Liejun did not flinch when Li lunged at him unsuccessfully - one last act of defiance. Something had to be done to avoid another round of war.

Bai Chongxi was arrested in his field headquarters while preparing to march against the Yue army, and Huang Xuchu seized in Nanning by Governor Huang Shaohong, who saw the writing on the wall. As Hu Hanmin arrived into the Presidential Palace, escorted by his leading supporters, he refused to give his defeated rival the dignity of seeing him in detention. Instead, as Ju Zheng and other Western Hills grandees looked on sheepishly, he reclaimed his place as Chairman, with fire in his eyes as the Gui government crumbles to dust. Standing defiantly in the capital, he dares any remaining challengers in the outlying provinces to face him and his wrath.

A winner was finally called, and the result was a stunning rebuke to Li Zongren and his power-grab. Ju Zheng, the champion of the party establishment, was named the victor and was promptly inaugurated to forestall any New Guangxi challenge. Their bitter triumph finally won, the Western Hills Clique took no chances: General Li was arrested before the convention was even adjourned. Bai was arrested in his field headquarters, Huang Xuchu seized in Nanning by Governor Huang Shaohong. Most of New Guangxi's soldiers followed Govenor Huang's example, choosing survival over loyalty.

With New Guangxi rebuffed, an intra-party civil war is likely to be avoided but not without difficult negotiations. As promised, Hu Hanmin and his Yue delegation arrived to negotiate terms in a solemn procession. Resentments continue, with mutual feelings of betrayal clouding discussions. Under pressure from his generals to seek a speedy resolution, Hu and his deputies acquiesced to terms largely in favour of the Gui government, recognising Ju as Chairman and formally dissolving the Yue committee. While all participants are happy to put the crisis behind them, its consequences continue to reverbate. We can only hope that this peace will hold.

Ju Zheng, the champion of the party establishment, was named the victor and was promptly inaugurated to forestall any New Guangxi challenge. Their bitter triumph finally won, the Western Hills Clique took no chances: General Li was arrested before the convention was even adjourned. The result determined, the junior ranks quickly fell in line as Li's house of cards collapsed in on itself. Bai was arrested in his field headquarters, Huang Xuchu seized in Nanning by Governor Huang Shaohong. Most of New Guangxi's soldiers followed Govenor Huang's example, choosing survival over loyalty.

With New Guangxi rebuffed, an intra-party civil war is likely to be avoided but not without difficult negotiations. As promised, Hu Hanmin and his Yue delegation arrived to negotiate terms to adoring crowds. Resentments continue, with mutual feelings of betrayal clouding discussions. With the Gui government largely discredited in the eyes of the general public and many applauding Hu for securing Li's ouster, Ju held a considerably weaker bargaining position. Realising the inevitable, Ju pressed for what terms he could in exchange for his recently gained position, stepping down as Chairman after negotiations to usher in Hu Hanmin's return. While all participants are happy to put the crisis behind them, its consequences continue to reverbate. We can only hope that this peace will hold.

paths.name: Remembering the First Republic — Salutations to Huang Fu and Political Science!
paths.shortName: Salutations to Huang Fu and Political Science!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Remembering the First Republic” becomes available, choose “Salutations to Huang Fu and Political Science!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The old Beiyang Republic was, by many accounts, a mess of contradictions. What should have been China's first steps towards Democracy and a brighter future was instead corrupted. However, not all who worked within Beiyang were traitors. Many were ardent Democrats trying their hardest to make the best of a bad situation, trapped by the corruption of those around them. It is natural for them to be sympathetic of course, for Western Hills owes its legacy to the Constitutional Club formed within the Beiyang political system by Zhang Ji and others.

Now that the Party-State has liberated China from Beiyang's corruption, it has also liberated these minds to work freely. But the concept of introducing them into our government directly or not, is another question entirely. Zhang Ji and Xu Chongzhi have correctly brought up that Feng Yuxiang and the Guominjun granted them their place of asylum, in the Westerns Hills of Beijing, which gave the clique its name in the first place. Insisting that not repaying such kindness would be remiss of the clique.

The Chairman himself has brought forth the interesting possibility of working with Beiyang Democrats, conservatives and the like. Those that remained idealistic in the dimming stranglehold of the Five Races. Whilst not necessarily Kuomintang, they nonetheless would serve a purpose once the period of Tutelage has ended, and the period of Constitutional Rule has begun.

Finally, and most attractive to the Western Hills Clique, is Li Liejun and Xie Chi's proposal. That of inviting the Kuomintang's fellow first sons; the Political Science Clique. Whilst it is true that Political Science long cast their lot with Beijing, even arranging multiple attempts to oust the Guofu, it is nonetheless admirable that Huang Fu, Gu Zhongxiu, Zhang Yaozeng, Li Genyuan and their old guard continued to trifle autocrats at every turn. They may be pariahs in the party, but so was Western Hills once upon a time.
objectives: When “Remembering the First Republic” becomes available, choose “Salutations to Huang Fu and Political Science!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Democratic Disappointment — Democracy Dies At the Ballot.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Democratic Disappointment” becomes available, choose “Democracy Dies At the Ballot.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

China's republicans had high hopes for the elections, but the light of Federalist democracy has been fading for some time. More and more races became one sided, fewer and fewer decisions made through public discourse, and consensus has increasingly become the product of bribery and coercion rather than debate and rhetoric. In retrospect the young republic pulling off any competitive electoral contests was a miracle, and one that will likely not be repeated this generation.

The China Democratic League ran an energetic campaign but amid growing public apathy at the process and the disillusionment of the political class their national fortunes rapidly ran out of steam. Their abrupt fall from public grace was accelerated by open infighting between their leaders, the defection of potential coalition partners, and an incoherent political message.

The Grand Republican Alliance naturally reaped the rewards, but the ultimate victor was not Chen Qiyou and the civilian dominated wing of the party but instead Ye Ju and his Yue Army Clique. With the nation preferring the return to strongman rule, the General was easily elected President with Zhong Xiunan as his running mate - assembling a cabinet of fellow Yue Army veterans, non-partisan technocrats, and some PIP luminaries.



Plenty of leading intellectuals are incensed by the democratic backsliding, but there is little they can do at this point but make token protests. The massive rallies the idealists hoped would materialise never did as most had long accepted the fate of the republic and kept their heads down. New Prime Minister Ma Yuhang and the Yue Clique government promises to restore stability to the republic and protect the constitution, but they too would be disappointed by the cold indifference of the general public.

paths.name: To Rule a Nation — General Ma Ji is a natural fit for the job.
paths.shortName: General Ma Ji is a natural fit for the job.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “To Rule a Nation” becomes available, choose “General Ma Ji is a natural fit for the job.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With his victory in China's wars of unification, President Lu Yuguang's position in China's new order has been sealed in blood. He has dispatched the last of his enemies in battle, driving out rival contenders for power and putting down any rebels that dared to challenge him. And with that, he has become the face of national unification - there remain dissenters but uncontested power has this tendency to smoothen out the rougher edges of a leader's image.

With that power comes the need to demonstrate leadership for the long fragmented nation. The President needs to set a long term direction for his regime, and it begins with his selection of Prime Minister. With confirmation at this point merely a formality, many would expect General Ma Ji to be the natural choice: an experienced general with Zhili connections and the pillar of the Young Guangxi Faction. Selecting him would indicate the desire of the Guangxi Warlords to replicate the Zhili system, supplanting Cao Kun and Wu Peifu with a new strongman junta that the rest of the republic will orbit around. But despite their ostensibly close alliance, Lu may have some reservations as well - Ma may be powerful enough to eclipse him already and many see him as an old guard choice.

There are many who have called for change in the name of the "Southern Spirit": now that the corrupt Beiyang Regime has been toppled, it would only be right for the new government to transition towards civilian rule. Ma Junwu, the long-time educator and old Tongmenghui revolutionary affiliated with the Guangxi cliques may fit this mold the best. Arrogant, conceited but respected by many for his work as a writer, industrialist, and teacher, he humbly claims to be uninterested in politics and prefers his books and poetry. But few expect him to turn down an offer for the Prime Ministership.
objectives: When “To Rule a Nation” becomes available, choose “General Ma Ji is a natural fit for the job.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Last Outing For Democracy — And the ballots ring out for Chen!
paths.shortName: And the ballots ring out for Chen!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Last Outing For Democracy” becomes available, choose “And the ballots ring out for Chen!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Despite their stewardship of Chinese Unification, few could try call themselves keen allies, or friends, of the Association of All Classes to Save Guangdong, or of the Merchants, or of the businessmen and industrialists. And even amongst those groups, few look fondly to Chen Lianbo, with his arrogance and incessant ambition. Constructing his own government, hardly comparable to most others within China, Chen has looked towards his roots in Guangzhou, and Hong Kong, seeking to institute what publicists have referred to as "Cantonese Style Democracy". Highly elitist, votes matter, but the voting participants are pretty much exclusively the wealthy and well-connected. Whilst ostensibly not too far from the democracy of Beiyang, the Old Republic at least carried with it the nominal pretences of free, fair, and equal elections, even if that wasn't the case in practice, it is still a significant step up, by almost codifying rule of the elite.

By significantly tightening the voting pool for elected representatives, those elected to the Assembly and Senate, who then vote for the President, are by far the old establishmentarians, and some of the new elites ushered by Chen. But for all of their grandeur, the Merchant's own sensibilites may be their own folly. With blatant favouritism to the South of the nation, and through the machinations of the Political Science Clique, a considerably developed loose alliance of figures have aligned to oppose the Merchants.

Rallying under the banner of War Hero Liu Zhenhuan, who's ambitions in Guangxi have made him short of a rival for Chen, Liu has managed to bring forward a motley crew of warlords, members of the Federation of Chinese Democratic Parties, and even occasional ex-revolutionaries to his cause. Running with Lin Zhengxuan as his candidate for Prime Minister, albeit unofficial until confirmed in office, the duo have managed to orchestrate an arrangement with other PSC figures such as Huang Fu, or Gu Zhongxiu, for affirmation of their roles in the cabinet, in-exchange for Clique unity.
objectives: When “Last Outing For Democracy” becomes available, choose “And the ballots ring out for Chen!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Death of Shen Hongying — The cultured Zhu Jiahua stages a soft coup to seize power!
paths.shortName: The cultured Zhu Jiahua stages a soft coup to seize power!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Death of Shen Hongying” becomes available, choose “The cultured Zhu Jiahua stages a soft coup to seize power!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Shen Hongying has been unwell for some time, and as victory celebrations around the nation die down and reconstruction begins, it seems that the republic's conquering Generalissimo's life also has come to an end. He is to be buried in a grand family tomb with various lots already prepared for his wives and concubines. His memorial service will be attended by millions, a massive turn of fortunes for a man who had a difficult road to power.

Among those attending his funeral are men hoping to take his place. When President Shen attempted to groom his son Shen Rongguang as his successor, the (relatively) young General is seen as too comparitively insignificant to take power right now. His father has died too soon, leaving the old Shen Army Faction in shambles.

Prime Minister Zhu Jiahua is as ruthless as a snake. Having built his own clique in the government, he is quickly utilising his Jingxing Society ties to win over the old Beiyang establishment, foreign emissaries, and curry a gentlemanly image to contrast with the "bandit" heritage of his rivals. Unlike those Guangxi "bumpkins" who spent all but a few years of their lives in a backwards province, the cosmopolitan Zhu grew up in Eastern China, studied abroad, and worked in both Beijing and Guangzhou. But his route to power ultimately hinges on swaying key powerholders like the two Yangs in the army, his rivals in the Political Science Clique, and fellow Jingxing affiliate Ma Junwu to shore up his Guangxi base.

Resisting this palace coup is the ambitious General Li Yaohan. His push for the Presidency faces difficult odds because he is from Guangdong and not particularly respected by the late Marshal Shen's Guangxi officers. Shen Rongguang however can generally count on the support of his father's people, who were generally tight-knit. If the two could ally fast enough, they may be able to seize control with the help of the PSC. But there are large egos and different generations involved.
objectives: When “The Death of Shen Hongying” becomes available, choose “The cultured Zhu Jiahua stages a soft coup to seize power!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Presidential Elections — Congratulations to Chen Jiongming / Chen Qiyou / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Dan Maoxin!
paths.shortName: Congratulations to Chen Jiongming / Chen Qiyou / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Dan Maoxin!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
Requires your country to be the United Provinces of China leader. When “The Presidential Elections” becomes available, choose “Congratulations to Chen Jiongming / Chen Qiyou / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Dan Maoxin!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The Presidential election has arguably been the most anticipated part of this election cycle. While various constitutions and other laws have sought to turn China into a parliamentary system, in practice China has always been Presidential in nature. And few Presidents have willingly left office.

The President is to be chosen indirectly, with the national assembly voting on China's next head of state. Although formal political parties in China have proliferated over the past decade or so, party loyalty remains limited among the rank and file. There will be plenty of opportunities for horse-trading with party leaders and to secure opportune defectors.

Afterwards, the new President will be expected to create a working government. Coalition talks are already underway between the third parties and the two camps, as the Presidential prospects seek to not only win support for themselves, but also their choice of Prime Minister. / The Presidential election has arguably been the most anticipated part of this election cycle. While various constitutions and other laws have sought to turn China into a parliamentary system, in practice China has always been Presidential in nature. And few Presidents have willingly left office.

The President is to be chosen directly, with millions of Chinese voters casting ballots for their preferred candidate. With leaders of the larger political parties wisely sitting out of the race in face of pressure, the vote will be won by one of two men. It has taken some time for the vote to be tabulated, however a new President is expected to be announced soon.

Afterwards, the new President will be expected to create a working government. Coalition talks are already underway between the third parties and the two camps, as the Presidential prospects seek to not only win support for themselves, but also their choice of Prime Minister.

paths.name: Assembly Elections Postponed Indefinitely — An unfortunate reality for our nation.
paths.shortName: An unfortunate reality for our nation.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
Requires your country to be the United Provinces of China leader. When “Assembly Elections Postponed Indefinitely” becomes available, choose “An unfortunate reality for our nation.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

After the exhausting first Federal elections, the Chinese political establishment had little appetite for another round of campaigning. Three years have passed and elections would normally be scheduled in a few months. However, there has been little movement in that direction over the past few weeks: no open campaigning or major candidate announcements.

Finally, the nation's leaders cautiously broke the silence. Chen Jiongming / Chen Qiyou / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Dan Maoxin, Zhang Junmai / Cun Shusheng / Luo Longji / Zhang Lan, and other senior leaders of major parties announced a joint decision to delay the next assembly election until after Chinese unification is complete - a controversial but perhaps understandable decision. There have been some protests over the delay, with opponents pointing to the suspension of the 1933 Assembly Elections as the clearest sign of the Zhili clique's reneging of their liberal promises after their initial unification.
objectives: Requires your country to be the United Provinces of China leader. When “Assembly Elections Postponed Indefinitely” becomes available, choose “An unfortunate reality for our nation.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

In a great parliamentary upset, Bill 7 is not passed, leading to the collapse of the government and another election. The Conservatives, under their new leader RB Bennet, are victorious.
In a response to the crisis in Québec, Bennet is ousted as prime minister. His successor restores the Unionist Party of Canada, eventually forming a broad coalition between hardliners, moderates and liberal-unionists within the party.
After the war, civilian rule is reinstated under the Conservatives.

paths.name: Death of Hugh Guthrie — Welcome Prime Minister Henry and Premier Hepburn.
paths.shortName: Welcome Prime Minister Henry and Premier Hepburn.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Death of Hugh Guthrie” becomes available, choose “Welcome Prime Minister Henry and Premier Hepburn.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Prime Minister of Canada, Hugh Guthrie, has died in office today. The Nation enters a day of mourning as he is laid to rest. His Minister of Finance, Nelson Edgar Rhodes, becoming Acting Prime Minister as the Unionist caucus debated on who to make the new Prime Minister.

After a surprisingly brief debate, the caucus came to the decision to make George Stewart Henry, current Premier of Ontario, the leader of their group and Prime Minister of Canada. Resigning from his seat in the Ontario Legislature and running for Guthrie’s old seat in Wellington South. In Ontario the Liberal-Unionist Mitchell Hepburn, leader of the Ontario Liberal Party, has controversially been made the new Premier in Ontario’s own Unionist Government between the two major parties, betraying Hepburn’s alliance with the CCF and UFO to topple the Conservative Government.

Despite this slight controversy, Prime Minister Henry has been sworn in to applause from the entire Unionist caucus, and should be a stable hand for the upcoming struggles that we still face. / Leader of the unofficial “Unionist” group in Parliament, Hugh Guthrie, has died today. A former Liberal who joined The Great War period Unionist Government due to his support of British Imperialism, Guthrie continued with the Conservative Party in the post war. Most famous for his reforms to manage the twin armed forces after the British Revolution, Guthrie quickly became the most high profile Unionist in Parliament. At different times being Minister of Justice, Attorney-General, Solicitor-General, and Minister of National Defence.

His death marks a notable weakening of the Unionists caucus, lacking a Parliamentary leader means the group has become more disorganised, granting us breathing room on our right flank. Despite his opposition to our leadership however, it’s not good of us to speak ill of the dead, and we should show kindness in this moment.

paths.name: Sinarquista Coup — Curse your sudden but inevitable betrayal.
paths.shortName: Curse your sudden but inevitable betrayal.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Sinarquista Coup” becomes available, choose “Curse your sudden but inevitable betrayal.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The Sinarquistas have shown their true colours. José Antonio Urquiza walked into Mexico City a hero. As he did so, he and the Gold Shirts marched straight towards the Palacio Nacional, and without a shot being fired, they seized the building. It seems that the soldiers rather would rather support the Sinarquistas over the Junta. With this bloodless coup, the Sinarquistas are now in charge of Mexico. They have promised that Mexico shall be restored to its proper glory and that rebels shall never threaten Mexico again.

paths.name: Restore Democracy? — Restore Democracy.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Restore Democracy?” becomes available, choose “Restore Democracy.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With our victory against the peasant rebels, we're finally in a position to look inwards at our government institutions and fully restore our pre-revolutionary government. However, it's unclear what path we should take. Mexico, for decades, prospered under the guidance of Porfirio Díaz, and while the benefits of his rule slowly waned in his final days, there's no denying that perhaps going back to those days with Garza in power could be beneficial. On the other hand, democracy has quickly become part of Mexican culture, and with liberal and conservative parties pressuring the Junta to restore at least some semblance of democratic rule, perhaps it would be best if, instead of a dictatorship, we pursued a slow transition towards democracy...
objectives: When “Restore Democracy?” becomes available, choose “Restore Democracy.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Victory for the Federal Government — ¡Viva Cristo Rey! ¡Viva México!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

The unthinkable has occurred, and today in Mexico City the banner of the Cristeros has flown alongside that of Mexico. They have taken control of the government and have promised to bring about a new and better Mexico. / Pancho Villa and Rubén Jaramillo have entered Mexico City as heroes. The military junta that has ruled Mexico since Zapata's death has been dissolved. They have stated that the ideals of the revolution have not died but have been tested and that they shall be working on safeguards to prevent another junta from coming about in the future. Furthermore, they have stated that they shall hold a new presidential election in the near future. / At long last, the terrorist army has been destroyed. While there are still some skirmishes in the country, order has at last been restored to Mexico. President The Leader is relieved that his enemies are finally destroyed. / The rebels have been dealt with, and order has been restored to the country. The Leader is celebrated throughout Mexico as a hero by most for ending the rebellion and restoring law and order to the country.
objectives: When “Victory for the Federal Government” becomes available, choose “¡Viva Cristo Rey! ¡Viva México!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.notes:
When “A New Era Dawns: The New State” becomes available, choose “Everything is proceeding as planned.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Following the ratification of new laws intended to empower the president, some elements within the military attempted to arrest the president though thankfully they were repelled by Loyalist elements. While some opponents claim this coup attempt was fabricated, it remains no doubt that Vargas is the most powerful man in Brazil since the days of the Empire. What he will do with this newfound power is the only question but it is obvious that his vision for Brazil has been influenced by many foreign thinkers, particularly of German nature. While Vargas has been lambasted by decentralist opponents, these opinions matter little to Vargas and his legions of supporters, as Brazil's reformation into a brand new state is complete... and perhaps irreversible.

Foul traitors have seized the presidential palace! After arresting President Mangabeira and declaring in a pronunciamento that they would not step down, the reactionary officers clearly miscalculated their strength in Rio, especially in terms of manpower. Leftist military men, worker's militia, anarchists and students, led by Isidoro Dias Lopes and Luis Carlos Prestes, not to mention civilian leaders, successfully seized barracks and the palace after a day of intense conflict... paths.name: The First Congress of Trade Unions — Autonomistas.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The First Congress of Trade Unions” becomes available, choose “Autonomistas.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

As we purged Brazil of its capitalistic junta, we now have to decide on our new leadership. Many local syndicalists already were based in Rio for political reasons, but the decision on how Brazil will head towards socialism is now up in the air, to be decided by the first congress of trade unions. Three main ideological factions arose in the small time we had to ponder and debate. The Orthodox Syndicalists are, as the name suggest, the ones that are attuned to foreign intellectuals and European syndicalism, while the Autonomists see the European governments as excessively large and centralised, and claim that Brazil is simply too large and varied to be administrated in such a way. The third faction, the Maximalists, are a minority by a large margin, but their loud cries for action and strong leadership resonate with some leaders. No matter who walks off this first congress in power, this choice is an irreversible one for the path that our nation must take in following decades, and thus many debates are being held, even as forces outside the state seek to push for counter-revolution.
objectives: When “The First Congress of Trade Unions” becomes available, choose “Autonomistas.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The Parti Socialiste de France, or Socialist Party of France, also known as the Jacobins, secure a majority in the elections of 1936, making way for their vision of a technocratic state according to the principles of the Constructive Revolution, with Adrien Marquet leading them in this endeavour.

The Jacobins manage to peacefully reform the system from within, and succeed in later elections.
paths.sourceStatus: Official game-rule option; not playtested
objectives: Follow the Jacobins - Marquet's Gradual Reform political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.name: Popular Front
paths.notes:
The Jacobins secure a majority in the elections of 1936. Jacobin hardliners then demand that syndicalist societal structures be abolished and the nation remade.

The reforms made by Jacobins upset many in French society, culminating in Civil War general Maurice Gamelin supporting Léon Blum's Popular Front of the Comités Syndicalistes Révolutionnaires. They remove the Jacobins from office, restoring the syndicalist status quo and ensuring their success in later elections.
paths.sourceStatus: Official game-rule option; not playtested
objectives: Follow the Popular Front political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.name: No Majority
paths.notes: No majority is found in the 1936 elections, and incumbent chairman Pierre Monatte leads a compromise Comités Syndicalistes Révolutionnaires government. Jacques Doriot takes over in 1941.
paths.sourceStatus: Official game-rule option; not playtested
objectives: Follow the No Majority political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Results: Orthodox Majority” becomes available, choose “Congratulations, Camarade Souvarine.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Even if many saw in this election the fall of the Orthodox-led consensus that has ruled the Commune since the death of Émile Pouget, they have managed to secure a firm majority in the election.

The Orthodoxes are now looking towards the Russian émigré Boris Souvarine, who unlike Pivert, is seen as both strong enough to keep the radical factions in line and capable of leading the Commune to its final glory!

The two favourites to succeed him are the trade unionist Léon Jouhaux and the civil war veteran Benoit Frachon.

paths.name: The End of the Chairmanship — Abolish the position, it's time for collective leadership!
paths.shortName: Abolish the position, it's time for collective leadership!

As the Anarchists have been swept to power during the last elections of the Commune and the Revolution Progresses, it has become obvious that reform must come to the highest positions as well. While previously the power of the Chairman was not unlimited, having one person lead the Commune is obviously a restrictive, bourgeoisie concept. It is a spit in the face of the ideas represented by the victorious Anarchists, who prefer a more communal leadership style.

Pierre Monatte, the Bourse Générale du Travail Chairman, has announced that he and the Assembly would elect a new Chairman itself to lead a compromise cabinet, and also to avoid deeper internal struggles between Jacobins and Sorelians.

paths.name: A Jacobin Reformation? — The old system shall be swept away!
paths.shortName: The old system shall be swept away!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

Having at long last taken control of the Commune, the Jacobin led Comité de Salut Public is now divided. Hardliners are demanding that the syndicalist structures be abolished, all replaced by a "Parti Unique" (Single Party) and a "Technician" State. However, this is likely to viciously divide France and as such many members of the party are suggesting that the Jacobins continue to operate within the established syndicalist structures of the BGT and CSP while gradually reforming the state along Constructive Revolutionary lines.

paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

The Front Populaire has seized Paris and is purging the Jacobins from the city. Communes throughout France have taken this opportunity to liquidate their own branches of the "Parti Unique". Gamelin and Blum have restored the formerly abolished syndicalist institutions, the CGT and BGT, and in emergency elections Gamelin has been elected as Chairman of the Bourse Générale du Travail with Blum appointed Chairman of the Comité de Salut Public.

The major issue is the re-integration in the Commune of former Social-Democrats that left fifteen years ago. The Orthodoxes, now the most reformist faction within the CGT, want to continue the democratisation process and push for an open arms policy towards the Social-Democrats. The Anarchists, although in favour of liberalisation, oppose that policy, as well as the now declining Sorelians. The Jacobins, of course, still advocate a technocratic reform.

paths.name: Federationists - Horner
paths.notes:
The Federationist faction of the Labour Party secure a majority in the Trade Union Congress of 1936.
The Hornerist tendency within the faction comes to the fore, as Arthur Horner becomes Chairman with George Hardy as his deputy, who is later replaced with G.D.H. Cole after the Second Weltkrieg.
objectives: Follow the Federationists - Horner political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.name: Autonomists - A New Capital
paths.notes:
The Autonomist faction of the Labour Party secure a majority in the Trade Union Congress of 1936. Niclas y Glais promises greater decentralisation for the people of Britain, and establishes Trade Union Congresses in Edinburgh and Cardiff.
In order to move away from the centralist tendencies of London, Birmingham is chosen as the new capital of Britain after the Second Weltkrieg, with Scotland and Wales being granted a large degree of autonomy.
objectives: Follow the Autonomists - A New Capital political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.name: Autonomists - Independence

The Autonomist faction of the Labour Party secure a majority in the Trade Union Congress of 1936. Niclas y Glais promises greater decentralisation for the people of Britain, and establishes Trade Union Congresses in Edinburgh and Cardiff.
After the Second Weltkrieg, y Glais fully dissolves the National Trade Union Congress of the Union of Britain, and forms a new English TUC, granting full independence to the new Scottish and Welsh TUCs. Ebenezer Edwards takes over as Chairman of the Union of England.

He claimed that in face of massive rifts within the TUC and due to his age he intends to resign his post immediately and have an interim committee take his place until the final ballots are cast. While Mann's Chairmanship has had its ups and downs, he is still a broadly popular figure within the TUC and Britain at large, being a titan of British Syndicalism. It is little surprise then that the delegation present at the Congress was quick to give the Chairman a standing ovation, with everyone from the Maximist militants to fringe Autonomist pacifists giving him his due.

It would appear that, while he was clearly planning on retiring once this Congress had run its course, the venerable Chairman Mann is the only man who can unite the fractured Labour Party in this critical time, as Arthur Horner's attempts to negotiate his own coalition have fallen on deaf ears. Deputy Chairman Mosley, perhaps humbled by his lack of success, has indicated that he is willing to retain the current Federationist-Maximist coalition even if the tensions between himself and Mann are well-known. On the other side of the isle, the Autonomists have also come out in favour of a coalition under the Chairman, putting forward Niclas y Glais as their candidate for the Deputy Chairmanship.

Ultimately, the choice falls on Mann's shoulders: does he stick by Mosley, or bring in the Autonomists?

paths.name: No Majority in the 1936 Election — Welcome, Reichskanzler Schleicher!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “No Majority in the 1936 Election” becomes available, choose “Welcome, Reichskanzler Schleicher!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

As predicted by quite a few during the campaign, no majority has been found in the Reichstag after the elections of 1936. A majority is impossible without the participation of either the SPD or the DVLP, two parties on different ends of the political spectrum, either of which would need time to dismantle the old consensus and craft a new coalition in the legislature. However, there is no time for the Reichstag to bicker amongst themselves until they finally form a government — with each passing day, the economic situation grows worse and the faith of the people falters further.

When the parliamentarians cannot lead, the duty to make a decision falls to the Kaiser, Wilhelm II. Even after the March Constitution, his role in the formation of governments remains definite, and whenever there is no obvious majority in the Reichstag, he has seen fit to appoint compromise choices like Brockdorff or loyalists of the court like Dirksen. Through Crown Prince Wilhelm, the Kaiser was recommended an interesting choice — Kurt von Schleicher, the current Minister of War of Prussia.

Ever since Leo von Caprivi's resignation in 1894, Wilhelm II has been reluctant to appoint military candidates to the office, and parliamentarians would hardly wish to see a uniformed man command the Empire either, as it brings back memories of Hindenburg and Ludendorff's plotting during the Weltkrieg. However, Schleicher offers several valuable qualities as well. During the past two decades, he has nurtured the image of a moderate who works well with the Reichstag, has ties and connections across the political spectrum and is a noted supporter of trade unions such as the ADGB, earning him the moniker "The Red General". At a time when national unity is necessary, all of these qualities are crucial. Finally, he is a close friend of Crown Prince Wilhelm, who is a major influence on his aged father and eventually got him to appoint the new Reichskanzler.
objectives: When “No Majority in the 1936 Election” becomes available, choose “Welcome, Reichskanzler Schleicher!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Schleicher Removed in Vote of No Confidence — The conclusion of decades of struggle...
paths.shortName: The conclusion of decades of struggle...
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Schleicher Removed in Vote of No Confidence” becomes available, choose “The conclusion of decades of struggle...”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The appointment of Kurt von Schleicher was a slap in the face for the Reichstag, who had been fostering a process of Parliamentarisation in the German Empire for the past few decades and yet suddenly saw their informal role in forming governments be challenged. As such, no matter if they were on the left or the right, the Reichstag began to plot, seeking to overthrow the Reichskanzler with the power of no-confidence vote granted to the Reichstag in the constitutional reforms of 1920.

The SPD and its allies, an informal alliance known as the "Democratic Union" (Demokratische Union), ultimately took the lead, forming a majority in the legislature and initiating a no-confidence vote, citing that the Reichskanzler could no longer manage the government under these conditions and must step down. Though Schleicher fought to the best of his ability, he was unable to break the will of the SPD, and he was forced out after a majority vote.

His role in history will thus be that of a mere interim period, an independent who led Germany for a few brief months before handing the reins over to the government of Hermann Müller. For the first time in the Empire's history, a Social Democrat has been begrudgingly appointed as the Reichskanzler - all of the Empire's resistance and conservatism could not stand against the march of history.

The appointment of Kurt von Schleicher was a slap in the face for the Reichstag, who had been fostering a process of Parliamentarisation in the German Empire for the past few decades and yet suddenly saw their informal role in forming governments be challenged. As such, no matter if they were on the left or the right, the Reichstag began to plot, seeking to overthrow the Reichskanzler with the power of no-confidence vote granted to the Reichstag in the constitutional reforms of 1920.

The DkP and the DVLP, joining forces in the "Black-White-Red" (Schwarz-Weiß-Rot) alliance, ultimately took the lead, forming a majority in the legislature and initiating a no-confidence vote, citing that the Reichskanzler could no longer manage the government under these conditions and must step down. Though Schleicher fought to the best of his ability, he was unable to overcome the conservative resistance, and he was forced out after a majority vote.

His role in history will thus be that of a mere interim period, an independent who led Germany for a few brief months before handing the reins over to the government of Ewald von Kleist-Schmenzin - an independent appointed to mediate between the two powerful coalition partners. For the first time in decades, a true conservative government leads Germany again - years of parliamentarisation, liberalism and reform could not hold back the reaction of the German conservatives, and they've returned with a vengeance.
objectives: When “Schleicher Removed in Vote of No Confidence” becomes available, choose “What will become of the golden constitution?”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Schleicher Out, SPD In — Was this their plan all along?
