paths.name: The Inauguration of Floyd Olson — Hail to the Chief.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Inauguration of Floyd Olson” becomes available, choose “Hail to the Chief.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With less than three weeks between the contingent election and the inauguration, horse-trading over the makeup of the incoming cabinet kicked into high gear. Meanwhile the strike wave of 1936 has shown little signs of stopping, and neither has the political violence engulfing the nation. Despite this, America was willing to stop for a day to listen to their new President speak. With all eyes upon him, he began his speech with the usual boilerplate statements calling for unity, promising a smooth transition, and also vowing to work with Vice President Roosevelt.

But Olson quickly took a more argumentative tone, saying that "a nation cannot be preserved which does not preserve its citizens. Industry is retrenching, reducing wages, lowering the standard of living, destroying buying power, and throwing more and more men and women on the streets to shift for themselves. Just how that is going to solve our economic problems is beyond understanding!".

All the while, the hapless establishment has done little. "Never have the Republican and Democratic parties, both nationally and locally, been quite so low in morale and so bankrupt in ideas as today. They have stood like men dazed, watching the parade go by, and not knowing what it is all about." To him, only decisive action could save the republic, decisive action was what he was elected to do, and therefore decisive action he will take.

To those accusing him of trampling on civil liberties in the process, Olson roared with questions of his own: "Whose liberty? Liberty for what purpose? Liberty of the Citizens' Alliance to arm thugs to shoot defenceless strikers in the back? Liberty of promoters of spurious stocks to fleece widows and orphans? Liberty of millionaires to escape taxation? Liberty to make slaves of workers and serfs of farmers? These are the individual liberties that these people mean!"

President Olson has a long, difficult road ahead of him, but it is clear that America is ready to chart a new path.

When “The Inauguration of William Borah” becomes available, choose “Hail to the Chief.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With less than three weeks between the contingent election and the inauguration, horse-trading over the makeup of the incoming cabinet kicked into high gear. Meanwhile the strike wave of 1936 has shown little signs of stopping, and neither has the political violence engulfing the nation. Despite this, America was willing to stop for a day to listen to their new President speak. With all eyes upon him, he began his speech with the usual boilerplate statements calling for unity, promising a smooth transition, and also vowing to work with Vice President Roosevelt.

But Borah would hardly be content with a generic speech. Nicknamed the "Great Opposer" for his outspoken stances in Congress, he is a famed orator compared to the great American statesmen Daniel Webster, Henry Clay, and John Calhoun.

With the nation in the midst of a crisis, Borah spoke for over two hours without notes - addressing topics ranging from political gridlock, the economic depression, social justice, domestic violence and even touching slightly on international affairs. Invoking American patriotism, he said that "if we have erred we have erred out of too much love for those things which from childhood you and we together were taught to revere," calling for a united effort towards change.

Despite this, he took a harder line on radicalism, quoting Lincoln's warning to "entertain no compromise; have none of it." He stated that "there is nothing that dies so hard and rallies so often as intolerance. The vices and passions which it summons to its support are the most ruthless and the most persistent harbored in the human breast. They sometimes sleep but they never seem to die. Anything, any extraordinary situation, any unnecessary controversy, may light those fires again and plant in our republic that which has destroyed every republic which undertook to nurse it."

To some, Borah's impassioned speech moved them to tears. To others, however, he spoke much but said little.

paths.name: The Inauguration of Alf Landon — Hail to the Chief.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Inauguration of Alf Landon” becomes available, choose “Hail to the Chief.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With less than three weeks between the contingent election and the inauguration, horse-trading over the makeup of the incoming cabinet kicked into high gear. Meanwhile the strike wave of 1936 has shown little signs of stopping, and neither has the political violence engulfing the nation. Despite this, America was willing to stop for a day to listen to their new President speak. With all eyes upon him, he began his speech with the usual boilerplate statements calling for unity, promising a smooth transition, and also vowing to work with Vice President Roosevelt.

Landon tried to give Americans a feeling of normalcy. He prayed for "Divine Guidance to make (him) worthy of the faith and the confidence which (they) have shown in (him)" and expressed his hope for "every man and woman in this nation to understand (his) every word, for (he) speak(s) of issues deeply concerning us all."

He declared that "the time has come to stop this fumbling with recovery" and that "the country is ripe for recovery." Praising American initiative, he pointed out that the American enterprises amount to billions of dollars and predicted that "once all this consumer demand is released, the problem will be not where to find work for the workers, but where to find workers for the work."

Landon continued by saying that "one of the signs of the ending of past depressions was the launching of new business ventures. It is true that most of them were small. Altogether, however, they provided work for many millions of people." The current depression has seen few new ventures however because "the small business man, the working man who would like to become his own boss - the average American - has hesitated to start out for himself. He lacks confidence in the soundness of Federal policy; he is afraid of what may come next."

He vowed to dispel this fear and "unshackle initiative and free the spirit of American enterprise." But many fear he will merely unshackle further radicalism instead.

paths.name: The Inauguration of Huey Long — Hail to the Chief.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Inauguration of Huey Long” becomes available, choose “Hail to the Chief.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With less than three weeks between the contingent election and the inauguration, horse-trading over the makeup of the incoming cabinet kicked into high gear. Meanwhile the strike wave of 1936 has shown little signs of stopping, and neither has the political violence engulfing the nation. Despite this, America was willing to stop for a day to listen to their new President speak. With all eyes upon him, he began his speech with the usual boilerplate statements calling for unity, promising a smooth transition, and also vowing to work with Vice President Roosevelt.

Long held little back, grimly noting that "people today are seeing their own children hungry, tired, half-naked, lifting their tear-dimmed eyes into the sad faces of fathers and mothers, who cannot give them food and clothing they both need, and which is necessary to sustain them, and that goes on day after day, and night after night, when day gets into darkness and blackness, knowing those children would arise in the morning without being fed, and probably go to bed at night without being fed."

He reminded the nation that he does not "propose to say that there shall be no rich men," only that "when one man gets more than he and his children and children's children can spend or use in their lifetimes, that then we shall say that such person has his share."

Controversially, he said that "they say they don't like my methods. Well, I don't like them either. I really don't like to have to do things the way I do. I'd much rather get up before the legislature and say, 'Now this is a good law and it's for the benefit of the people, and I'd like you to vote for it in the interest of the public welfare.' Only I know that laws ain't made that way. You've got to fight fire with fire."

The new President closed by saying that his voice "will be the same as it has been", regardless of patronage, fear, or persecution. But whether or not that should draw praise or fear has increasingly polarised the nation.

paths.name: Midnight — God help us all.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Midnight” becomes available, choose “God help us all.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

For the past two weeks, Congress has been locked in an endless gridlock. No party or group has been willing or able to compromise in order to create a majority needed to elect a president or a vice president. As the country descends into rioting, mass strikes, and political violence, the election continues to be uncertified, preventing the election of either a president or a vice president.

Yesterday, previous Speaker John Nance Garner made one last desperate push to form a working coalition. With his own party conference unwilling to agree to commit their support to any presidential ticket however, his attempt failed just as all his previous ones had. It was now certain that, come the 20th, there would be no elected president to take office.

President Smith has had two weeks to prepare his administration for this eventuality. His solution has been to ask his cabinet not to hand in their resignations (conventionally done upon the inauguration of a new president), and to instead stay in their current positions until a new president is elected. As a result, at 12:00 noon, January 20th, 1937, when Smith was to leave office, Cordell Hull, the incumbent Secretary of State, would become acting president, as per the Presidential Succession Act of 1886.

Today that time has come. At noon, Former President Al Smith left office without a successor, leaving the office vacant for the first time in nearly 150 years. Immediately, Cordell Hull entered the Oval Office as the Acting President of the United States.

paths.name: Olson Falls Into a Coma — Oh god.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Olson Falls Into a Coma” becomes available, choose “Oh god.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

For several years now, President Olson has known that his time on Earth is limited. Always plagued with pain and health issues, Olson was finally diagnosed with stomach cancer, a fact which was carefully hidden from the public both during his time in the Senate and in the White House. Though he was in immense pain in the later stages of his career, Olson powered on through, acting as a workaholic both on the campaign trail and in office.

Olson's health has finally caught up to him, however. As his cancer has taken a turn for the worse, Olson has been hospitalised and has now fallen into a coma, from which his doctors doubt he will ever wake.

The sudden absence of the president due to previously unknown health issues has thrown the government into chaos: with no legal mechanism to replace a living but incapacitated president, the executive has been rendered headless for the time being. Meanwhile, speculation as to potential conspiracies has spread like wildfire, with many socialists speculating that the president has been poisoned by the capitalists.

paths.name: War Plan White Activated — The die is cast.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “War Plan White Activated” becomes available, choose “The die is cast.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Over the past few weeks, it has become abundantly clear that Acting President Hull's caretaker administration is incapable of restoring order to the country. The federal government has all but lost control completely in both the Midwest and Deep South, as state governments loyal either to the Socialist Party or Huey Long assert control over federal employees and National Guard units. The continuing failure of Congress to elect either a speaker or a president has sent the federal government's position into a death spiral, as Hull's legitimacy falls further and further.

With the writing on the wall, Acting President Hull has reluctantly heeded the advice of General Douglas MacArthur. War Plan White, the military counterinsurgency plan intended for an eruption of overwhelming domestic unrest, has been activated, with some modifications.

Additionally, Hull has chosen to step down as acting president in favour of MacArthur: he has appointed MacArthur as Secretary of State and conditioned his own resignation from that post on his successor's confirmation. The Senate, increasingly dominated by conservative voices, approved MacArthur's appointment, making him acting president.

Few have any illusions about MacArthur's new role. Open conflict between the federal government and radical political forces is now inevitable. Now, all we can do is brace ourselves for the coming storm.

paths.name: The End of the Union Party — It was never going to last.
paths.shortName: It was never going to last.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The End of the Union Party” becomes available, choose “It was never going to last.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The beginning of the Civil War has seen the national political landscape shift decisively back in favour of establishment political forces. As the nation unites behind the president and his establishment allies, Huey Long has been forced to adapt to remain politically relevant. The civil war as well has limited the room for any domestic opposition within the "White" camp, as the establishment parties consolidate control over the war effort and suppress out-of-line right-wing radicals.

As the Union Party was initially a mere electoral vehicle for Long's 1936 presidential bid, it was neither a proper mass party or even a strong congressional one. Many Democrats who endorsed Long's bid for the White House, such as Burton K. Wheeler, declined to identify themselves with it in Congress, instead choosing to remain Long-aligned Democrats. Recognising this, Long has now chosen to fully return to the Democratic fold, once again identifying as a Democrat.

What remains is the extra congressional element of the party, mainly consisting of Long's associates in the Share Our Wealth movement and other satellite groups. Most notable among these is Reverend Gerald L. K. Smith, the former director of the Share Our Wealth clubs who Long fired just a few weeks ago, citing "irreconcilable differences". Since his firing, Smith has started a new organisation called the America First Committee with like-minded former Union Party rightists, such as Charles Lindbergh. Smith and Lindbergh have, as time goes on, increasingly dispensed with Long's economic programme in favour of a national populist and laissez faire one, emphasising issues of race to an extent not embraced by Long.

Though this ideological change has given the AFC initial momentum, and rendered it ideologically coherent and acceptable to far-right business interests, it has not succeeded in remaining in the public spotlight. Instead, Long's return to the Democrats has received more attention, as speculation about a presidential bid in 1940 ramps up.

paths.name: Terra Moves to Suspend the Constitution Indefinitely — Terra succeeds and becomes President for Life!
paths.shortName: Terra succeeds and becomes President for Life!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Terra Moves to Suspend the Constitution Indefinitely” becomes available, choose “Terra succeeds and becomes President for Life!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Gabriel Terra has moved to bring an end to Uruguayan democracy it seems. Many politicians and military leaders have rallied behind him in what many have seen as a self-coup to destroy democracy and to make Terra president for life. There is much resistance to Terra's self-coup, mainly from Terra's own party, the Partido Colorado. The question is, will Terra's self-coup succeed, or will rival politicians be able to restore order in Montevideo?

With news of the collapse of the Berlin Stock Market reaching Venezuela and already affecting the economy, there have been numerous disturbances in Caracas and other cities as a run to the banks led to protests and riots. Many in the military believe that the Socialist Party is behind many of these disturbances and plan to use them to start a revolution in Venezuela. paths.name: The Governor-General's Coup — Long live the King! God save the West Indies Federation!
paths.shortName: Long live the King! God save the West Indies Federation!

When “The Governor-General's Coup” becomes available, choose “Long live the King! God save the West Indies Federation!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

As the socialist current encroached on the West Indies, the Governor-General kept receiving more and more complaints from his Majesty's most loyal subjects. More and more calls for equality and wealth distribution have muffled the cries for help of the people who helped the Crown most.

As the country has drifted further and further apart from the Crown, the Governor-General has made a hard choice today. He elected to listen to the demands of the few loyalists left in the federation and moved in with the army to replace the democratically elected government. Martial law has been declared, and steps have started to be taken to revert the most damaging reforms.

paths.name: Elections Restarted — The Parti pour l'Autonomie steals the polls!
paths.shortName: The Parti pour l'Autonomie steals the polls!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Elections Restarted” becomes available, choose “The Parti pour l'Autonomie steals the polls!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The socialist revolution has succeeded and the West Indies Union declared. Now that the rule of the socialism is safe within the West Indies, elections have restarted and the people have taken to the ballots. There are three major candidates -

The British Citizens' and Workers' Home Rule Party, more commonly known as the Butler Party (BP), under Tubal Uriah Butler and his clique, who aim for a higher position for trade unions in the West Indian Government. Butler's supporters are largely British socialists from Trinidad.

The People's Party (PP), under Aimé Fernand David Césaire, consisting of mainly French socialist youth who wish to see maximum autonomy for all provinces within the Union.

The Parti pour l'Autonomie (PA), now separated from the radical PNP after the revolution and led by Joseph Lagrosillière, aiming for a somewhat democratic system of political parties and consisting of mainly French citizens and Jamaican English politicians.
objectives: When “Elections Restarted” becomes available, choose “The Parti pour l'Autonomie steals the polls!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The Parti pour l'Autonomie (PA), now separated from the radical PNP after the revolution and led by Joseph Lagrosillière, aiming for a somewhat democratic system of political parties and consisting of mainly French citizens and Jamaican English politicians.

paths.name: The Coup — We must save Belarus from syndicalism!
paths.shortName: We must save Belarus from syndicalism!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Coup” becomes available, choose “We must save Belarus from syndicalism!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Many of Minsk's residents woke up this morning to soldiers patrolling the streets, ordering people to stay home. In front of Government House, where Sojm sessions are held, an armoured car and a platoon of soldiers watch over Independence Square, while the capital's radio stations were also occupied and had their regular transmission interrupted. Later in the morning, the First National Station broadcasted a message by Radaslau Astroŭski, Sojm delegate for the BSDP. Astroŭski announced that Taraškievič's government had been deposed by the army for collusion with "foreign, syndicalist elements", planning to subvert the deadlocked Sojm through a revolution. Furthermore, he announced that the presidency and the Council of People's Minister were replaced by a new temporary authority, the Belarusian Central Council, or Central Rada, with himself as its chairman. After the composition of the Rada was declared, he ended the message by issuing the order to arrest Taraškievič and other members of the former government for high treason.

While all roads going in and out of Minsk had military checkpoints by noon, it was clear that all members of the former government had avoided arrest and had fled the city. White Ruthenia appeared on the path of civil war.
objectives: When “The Coup” becomes available, choose “We must save Belarus from syndicalism!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Łastoŭski's Putsch — Long live the Kryvich State!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Łastoŭski's Putsch” becomes available, choose “Long live the Kryvich State!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With support for the Central Rada collapsing, Łastoŭski made his move. Leading a procession of supporters and members of the Union of Belarusian Youth, the head of the Kryvian movement marched into Government House in Minsk, with soldiers letting the marchers in without any resistance. With the army and the Germans abandoned him, Astroŭski had already fled the building before Łastoŭski's arrival, and the Kryvians quickly proclaimed the Central Rada deposed and the formation of a new Council of People's Ministers. Łastoŭski was proclaimed interim President and Chairman of the Council through a radio address, which included promises to restore the Constitution and the Sojm, though it remains to be seen who will be allowed to sit or if elections will be held. What is known is that Łastoŭski has promised to rid Belarus of its "Russian-hypnosis" once and for all and lead the revival of the Belarusian nation into its purest form, as Kryvians.
objectives: When “Łastoŭski's Putsch” becomes available, choose “Long live the Kryvich State!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

A new government has been formed, with support from both the army and the German military mission. It appears it will only be a matter of time before the remnants of the former government will be silenced and resistance in the countryside suppressed.

One of the fundamentals of being a democratic state is to hold elections every couple of years to let the people express their opinion on the government and a myriad of issues. This year is no different and the elections of are upon us. While many parties are vying for power across the country, everyone expects the BSDP to be able to smoothly sail to yet another electoral victory.

The polls have closed and the winner is...

As the Central Rada failed to defeat the rebels on their own, the German military mission began their own "anti-partisan operation" in White Ruthenia. In the process, however, they have taken direct control of all military forces and affairs in the country, with Werner Kempf becoming the virtual military dictator over the country with the creation of the Generalgouvernement Minsk. Astroŭski's Central Rada maintains control of civilian affairs but has effectively become subordinate to Governor-General Kempf. This is a serious humiliation and White Ruthenia has lost significant sovereignty in the process.

paths.name: Belarus Joins the International — The Belarusian Revolution enters a new stage!
paths.shortName: The Belarusian Revolution enters a new stage!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Belarus Joins the International” becomes available, choose “The Belarusian Revolution enters a new stage!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Our offer has been accepted by the revolutionaries of Europe and we have been accepted into the Third Internationale. Of course, there are caveats in this deal, as we have to quickly prove that we are indeed a true revolutionary regime ourselves.

An emergency session of the Belarusian Peasants' and Workers' Hramada was held, formally sanctioning the government's plan to make peace with the International and make efforts to join them. This was quickly followed by an emergency of the Sojm, rapidly passing a set of laws formally renouncing our ties with the fallen German Empire and announcing the government's intention to re-align the nation with the Syndicalist powers. Finally, a resolution was passed calling for the creation of a constitutional committee and the Sojm's dissolution.
objectives: When “Belarus Joins the International” becomes available, choose “The Belarusian Revolution enters a new stage!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

As war dawns once again on Europe, Taraškievič knows that the time has come for his final decision, on whether or not to follow through on the previous agreement with the Russians.

Does he lead his country to side with the Internationale, to socialism, and to further autonomy with more of his nation united under the government? Or does he stay true to the Germans, who have tolerated and supported his rule so far?

As part of this transition of power back into local civilian hands, a rump Sojm is to be reconvened, the Constitution restored, and the appointment of Adam Stankievič as interim President. In other words, the NDA's petition has been a complete success, with democracy truly restored instead of the hated Rada being given power once more.

paths.name: Coup — We have to believe in Jin.
paths.shortName: We have to believe in Jin.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Coup” becomes available, choose “We have to believe in Jin.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

As the situation began to hit Jin Shuren during the investigation, he's realised the position he is in. There will be no new governor for months at least along with no Yang Zengxin, and he is the most prominent government official left within Dihua currently. He needed to make his move before anyone else arrived, using his recently made army that was supposed to crush the Mongol bandits.

And as expected, he did. Jin Shuren with his 3,000 troops have stormed the capital and secured it completely, declaring himself governor of Xinjiang before a proper response from the Qing could even be formulated. Not all are pleased by these events, especially the Dao-yin of Aksu, Fan Yaonan, leading many to believe that crisis could be on its way to Xinjiang for the first time in 20 long years. Not only that, but it's not even known what the Qing will think about this turn of events, leaving Jin with absolute power over the entirety of Xinjiang until news is heard.
objectives: When “Coup” becomes available, choose “We have to believe in Jin.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Party — To Fan Yaonan, our new leader!
paths.shortName: To Fan Yaonan, our new leader!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Party” becomes available, choose “To Fan Yaonan, our new leader!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The night was lively as Yang Zengxin entered Aksu today, seeing mass amounts of food and drink for the night, ready to spend this night to the fullest as if it will be his last. He sits down an hour later, ready to finally begin. He digs into his food as Fan Yaonan and a multitude of other governmental officials join him in the luxuries of life. Fan excuses himself from the table with Yang barely noticing, still indulging his gluttony. Fan Yaonan returned ten minutes later, with two guards with guns and red arm bands in tow behind him as he sits down again.

"A toast, to Yang's continued health!"

Yang raised his glass as well, a smile on his face until he realised what was happening. The guards now pointed their guns as Yang, and shots immediately rang out in the banquet, and soon there was a dead, soiled, and decrepit Yang Zengxin lying on the ground with bullet holes in his head and chest.
objectives: When “The Party” becomes available, choose “To Fan Yaonan, our new leader!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Second Takeover — I'll pass on the banquet this time.
paths.shortName: I'll pass on the banquet this time.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

Jin secured Dihua and quickly moved onto Aksu, where Fan Yaonan waited, desperately trying to set up as many defences as he could before Jin would arrive. It was pointless, as when Jin arrived, soon after his securing of Dihua, his massive army rushed into the city and secured it all, eventually breaking through into Fan's residence, with Fan nowhere to be found. Before the Qing even knew their loyal governor Yang was gone, two coups have taken place in Xinjiang. Now Jin Shuren has installed himself as governor, and there is little Beijing can do about it.
objectives: When “The Second Takeover” becomes available, choose “I'll pass on the banquet this time.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

As many predicted, Jin Shuren has decided to make his move on Dihua and secure it using his newly armed force. The streets are filled with soldiers as any possible political dissidents are being removed one by one. Among these is the Dao-yin of Aksu, Fan Yaonan who has a somewhat petty rivalry with Jin. Little is known about what Jin's next moves will be, but many predict that Fan Yaonan's position of power will not be lasting for much longer.
objectives: When “Jin Shuren Secures Dihua” becomes available, choose “We lie in his hands...”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.shortName: Now these are the radical changes Xinjiang needs!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

As many predicted, Jin quickly moved from Dihua to remove Fan Yaonan's position in power before he could even act. Many noticed what looks like the beginning of a build-up of defences, but Fan's accomplices were killed before any meaningful resistance could be put up, though Fan himself could not be found. Some believe him to have escaped into the mountains to avoid capture. Ma Shaowu, the Dao-yin of Hotan has declared his loyalty to the new governor Jin Shuren, aiming to secure his rule in the south. Jin Shuren has agreed to this, finally achieving his rule over all of Xinjiang, at least for now.
objectives: When “Jin's March on Aksu” becomes available, choose “Now these are the radical changes Xinjiang needs!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

With Fan Yaonan's overthrow, the position of Dao-yin of Aksu has been empty. Out of the multitude of candidates including Jin Shuren's personal acquaintances, Sheng Shicai, the current Chief of Staff has ultimately been chosen for the position. Currently wielding a moderately sized army and having an even more competent chain of connections within the government, Jin was what many considered backed into a corner to this pick, but Sheng has promised that he will hold the utmost respect for the position and the weight it has.

paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

Jin Shuren marched out of his quarters, confident in his new plan to end the Kumuliks and Uyghur nationalists and bring order back to his rule. However, his march was closed off sooner then he expected, quickly stopped by his own guards, being forced to the pavement and dragged away from his home. He woke in the place he expected to be, the government capital, still being restrained by his guards. In front of him, Sheng Shicai, wielding a rifle. Without a word, Sheng points his rifle at Jin, as Jin begs for mercy among who he assumed was his most loyal subject. This fell upon deaf ears much to Jin's dismay, as the muzzle lit up and shot him, with Sheng's face being the last thing Jin saw in his lifetime.

Sheng Shicai has been installed as the new governor of Xinjiang, having overwhelming support from his fellow administrators including Ma Shaowu. Ready to bring Xinjiang into a new future, Sheng is ready to march unto the scene and end this pointless chaos once and for all.
objectives: When “Sheng Shicai's Army Coup” becomes available, choose “For a new start!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

As another meeting began in the Kashgar government between Ma Shaowu, Mahmut Muhti, and Burhan Shahidi on the composition of the government, something... unexpected occurred. The entire building they were in began to catch fire, with them barely being able to escape due to forewarning from lower members of government. They already knew the reason behind this, as this was no accident, but the workings of Sheng to remove his remaining political rivals once and for all. The three men under Ma Shaowu rode north with a small regiment in the hopes of being able to overthrow Sheng swiftly before he has time to react. This is their last resort as the fate of Xinjiang lies on the table, but whether such a desperate gambit can even succeed is another question.
objectives: When “The Purge of Uyghur Soldiers” becomes available, choose “Sheng is overthrown in Aksu.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Sheng's Purge Fails — Maybe we shouldn't have given them so many resources...
paths.shortName: Maybe we shouldn't have given them so many resources...
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:

What Sheng heard was going to be a meeting between Ma Shaowu, Mahmut Muhti, and Burhan Shahidi was currently under way in Kashgar, but something... unexpected occurred. While Sheng's plan was to set fire to the building and end his three greatest threats once and for all, none of them were in the building. In fact, the entire building was empty, without a trace of any soul. All of this was in the report given to Sheng, as panic began to set in over the whereabouts of his three rivals. He would meet them sooner then expected however, as them and their army soon surrounded Aksu before Sheng could react. Sheng had been betrayed, as his own northern government was infiltrated by agents of the three men allowing this plot to occur. Sheng has no choice but to surrender, leaving him to be imprisoned with his fate decided at a later point, as Shaowu now rules over Xinjiang in his Triumvirate alongside Mahmut Muhti and Burhan Shahidi.
objectives: When “Sheng's Purge Fails” becomes available, choose “Maybe we shouldn't have given them so many resources...”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: The Federalist Outpost
paths.notes:
Federalist Governor Tang Jiyao, the "King of Yunnan", and his forces overrun Kuomintang forces in Guizhou and secure their northeastern flank. They then prepare to make their move on Guangzhou either seizing it for themselves, or submitting to an aligned Federalist government.
Either way, Tang Jiyao rules through the Tang Pai, or Tang Jiyao's Clique, a web of connections that include his own People's Government Party, his gentrymen and army commanders, and various intellectuals affiliated with Southwestern University.
paths.sourceStatus: Official game-rule option; not playtested
objectives: Follow the The Federalist Outpost political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.name: A Nationalist Junta
paths.notes:
The Kuomintang operating out of Guizhou rout the Yunnan Army, and in desperation Tang Jiyao's commanders turn on him - allowing General Zhu Peide and the Guomindang - Guomingemingjun Di San Jun (Youpai), or Kuomintang - 3rd Army of the National Revolutionary Army (Rightists), to assume de facto leadership over the southwest.
He and other Kuomintang commanders then gear up to bring the revolution to Guangzhou, either seizing it for themselves, or submitting to an aligned Kuomintang government.
The various factions within the Kuomintang, including old right, new right, and the left also begin to scheme among themselves as the old Yunnan gentry reels.
paths.sourceStatus: Official game-rule option; not playtested
objectives: Follow the A Nationalist Junta political outcome. Consult the route conditions above before starting.

paths.name: Government by Efficiency
paths.notes:
Long Yun attempts to take advantage of the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War to consolidate power in Yunnan, and he successfully crushes domestic opposition.
Should Yunnan end up unifying the country, President Long Yun appoints a cabinet consisting of technocrats, close political allies, and family members - most notably his brothers in law. This cements the Long Pai, or Long Yun's Clique, and his personal power as the nation's new benevolent autocrat.

The Presidential election has arguably been the most anticipated part of this election cycle. While various constitutions and other laws have sought to turn China into a parliamentary system, in practice China has always been Presidential in nature. And few Presidents have willingly left office.

The President is to be chosen indirectly, with the national assembly voting on China's next head of state. Although formal political parties in China have proliferated over the past decade or so, party loyalty remains limited among the rank and file. There will be plenty of opportunities for horse-trading with party leaders and to secure opportune defectors.

Afterwards, the new President will be expected to create a working government. Coalition talks are already underway between the third parties and the two camps, as the Presidential prospects seek to not only win support for themselves, but also their choice of Prime Minister. / The Presidential election has arguably been the most anticipated part of this election cycle. The President is to be chosen directly, with millions of Chinese voters casting ballots for their preferred candidate. With leaders of the larger political parties wisely sitting out of the race in face of pressure, the vote will be won by one of two men. It has taken some time for the vote to be tabulated, however a new President is expected to be announced soon.

Afterwards, the new President will be expected to create a working government. Coalition talks are already underway between the third parties and the two camps, as the Presidential prospects seek to not only win support for themselves, but also their choice of Prime Minister.

paths.name: Assembly Elections Postponed Indefinitely — An unfortunate reality for our nation.
paths.shortName: An unfortunate reality for our nation.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

After the exhausting first Federal elections, the Chinese political establishment had little appetite for another round of campaigning. Three years have passed and elections would normally be scheduled in a few months. However, there has been little movement in that direction over the past few weeks: no open campaigning or major candidate announcements.

Finally, the nation's leaders cautiously broke the silence. Chen Jiongming / Chen Qiyou / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Dan Maoxin, Zhang Junmai / Cun Shusheng / Luo Longji / Zhang Lan, and other senior leaders of major parties announced a joint decision to delay the next assembly election until after Chinese unification is complete - a controversial but perhaps understandable decision. There have been some protests over the delay, with opponents pointing to the suspension of the 1933 Assembly Elections as the clearest sign of the Zhili clique's reneging of their liberal promises after their initial unification.

paths.name: A New Federalist Government — Federalism rises again.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “A New Federalist Government” becomes available, choose “Federalism rises again.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

After several weeks of deliberations, the final outline of this latest Guangzhou Government has taken shape. It will be built along Federalist lines, vowing to respect provincial autonomy and unite the provinces - through diplomacy first, by force if necessary. Tang Jiyao naturally assumed the Presidency after a speedy vote, he also named Chen Jiongming as his Vice President to appease the Cantonese Federalists.

A provisional legislature has been established, and Zhang Taiyan tasked with organising them as Prime Minister. Despite their similarities, there have already been some clear differences in their governing philosophies. Tang has advocated for a stronger central government, capable of fighting foreign imperialism and that can also play referee between the different provinces. Zhang has at times called for the near abolishment of the central government, arguing that China is too large to manage and prior central governments were prone to selling out to foreign powers - he has sought to empower the various provinces instead. Chen and most others have adopted a more moderate stance between them, and the new government is expected to operate as a compromise between the two extremes, held together by common fears of external attack.

There are many challenges ahead for the new government. The provinces across China are taking sides in the looming battle for reunification. Many question whether or not the Federalist regime will be able to resolve its internal contradictions, and whether they can do so peacefully.

paths.name: The Canton Compromise — A great act of statesmanship by both sides.
paths.shortName: A great act of statesmanship by both sides.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Canton Compromise” becomes available, choose “A great act of statesmanship by both sides.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

After several weeks of the Conference seemingly going nowhere, General He Yingqin of the First Army and leading party theoretician Dai Jitao of the Zhejiang Society of Revolutionary Comrades has struck an agreement, outflanking the previously dominant Moscow Committee and Third Army Clique. Under their proposal, General He will assume the Presidency of the Revolutionary Government, Chairman of the Kuomintang, and Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission while Dai Jitao will become the first Premier of the (provisional) Executive Yuan and Deputy Chairman of the Party, controlling the executive branch of the government as effectively a Prime Minister.

He Yingqin, who has gotten along shockingly well with Huang Shaohong and to a lesser extent Li Zongren and Bai Chongxi of the New Guangxi Clique, has managed to secure their support for the proposal. Huang is expected to be named Minister of the Interior as part of the arrangement, with favourable appointments to Li and Bai who still de facto control Guangxi along with Huang Xuchu.

Dai Jitao in turn has been able to convince Hu Hanmin and his allies not to walk out of the conference, leaning on their past friendship and an offer to make Hu Hanmin Premier of the (provisional) Legislative Yuan and Ju Zheng Premier of the (provisional) Judicial Yuan. He has sworn to work to uphold civilian rule and that this arrangement will be a temporary matter until unification.

Though far from a perfect setup, the fact that any consensus was found brought a relief to most delegates, who quickly fell in line with the He-Dai government. The herculean horsetrading that was required however bodes poorly for the long term prospects of this government, and it is clear that things are far from over.

paths.name: The White Sun Returns to Nanjing — We will work to incorporate their ideas.
paths.shortName: We will work to incorporate their ideas.

Requires your country to be the Left Kuomintang leader. When “The White Sun Returns to Nanjing” becomes available, choose “We will work to incorporate their ideas.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Nanjing was the site of Sun Yat-sen's glorious return to China, selected as the provisional president by the assembled revolutionaries there on January 12th, 1912. Today, The Leader proudly stands before the Nanjing Presidential Palace (formerly the Governor-General's Palace), delivering a speech to commemorate the National Revolutionary Army's victory.

With Nanjing's fall, the prospects of the left wing of the Kuomintang have fallen with it. The right, long seen as the weaker and less legitimate wing, is now in shambles and many of those wavering between the different wings have committed to the rightist regime. The largest of these defectors is the Reconstruction Faction (RCF), and their ever valuable figurehead Sun Fo has sworn loyalty to the rightist committee in order to claim his Central Executive Committee seat.

Sun Fo's RCF is the latest iteration of his circle, which began when he was Mayor of Guangzhou under his father Sun Yat-sen. Then known as the Crown Prince's clique, it included many younger technocrats and liberals who studied abroad. Though initially showing interest in the Western Hills Conference, they were cowed by Wang Jingwei into submission and later fled to Hawaii after the collapse of the Northern Expedition. This "Hawaii Clique" published a magazine known as the Reconstruction Review (which became their namesake) and also continues to hold ties across Chinese diaspora communities in Southeast Asia.

Sun Fo may have gotten his "inheritance", but whether or not his followers will receive any favourable positions besides token sinecures in the Legislative Yuan (Sun is already in talks to become Vice Premier) is another question. The bureaucracy is already quite competitive, and it will be up to the Political Science, Moscow Committee, and CC Cliques to make room for them.

paths.name: The Fallen Triumvir — Wang Jingwei can return but he better deliver.
paths.shortName: Wang Jingwei can return but he better deliver.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

Requires your country to be the Left Kuomintang leader. When “The Fallen Triumvir” becomes available, choose “Wang Jingwei can return but he better deliver.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Wang Jingwei and his Reorganisation Comrades Association (RCA) are the hated rivals of both the Old Right and the New Right, fierce competitors during Guangzhou's power games and seen as sellouts to the Third Internationale. Wang Jingwei is a proven political survivor however, flexible as he is arrogant, and is eager to worm his way back into the party's good graces - ostensibly in the name of party unity.

In reality, the RCA's relationship to The Leader is, in all regards, a highly complicated matter. With various individuals within the the country continuously flirting between the Left and Right wings, few prove particularly stringently opposed to Wang on ideological grounds. Many, if not all, support the 1924 Reorganisation, albeit few support an alliance with the International or cooperation with the Chinese Syndicalist Party, but instead provoke the need for party unity in dire times. Whilst this perhaps falls directly into the RCA's desires, the most stringent opposition arriving from men such as Li Genyuan has, rather paradoxically, induced more within the ranks to support Wang's efforts to reconcile.

Unlike the left, the right wing of the Kuomintang sees the end goal of the revolution as building a harmoniously cooperative national body, bound together by culture, acting in concert against mutual threat. Men like Dai Jitao, Hu Hanmin and Chiang Kai-shek saw themselves as truly revolutionaries despite their conservatism, and it is no surprise the left and right regularly branded each other as counterrevolutionary. In-between this resides men such as Zhu Peide, Chen Cheng, and Sun Fo. Men who, for one reason or another, advocate for and endorse the need for revolution, but are intent on reconciling both the left and right wing's outlooks.

For his part, Wang insists that he can still secure foreign support via backchannels if he is invited into government, and his presence will diminish support for the CSP. And on a global scale, Wang remains a leading face in the Kuomintang, it would be a strong message to refuse him. / Wang Jingwei and his Reorganisation Comrades Association (RCA) are the hated rivals of both the Old Right and the New Right, fierce competitors during Guangzhou's power games and seen as sellouts to the Third Internationale. While Dai approved the vanguardism of the 1924 Reorganisation, he argued that a true revolution could only be enacted via the masses rather than a radical minority and disapproved of the alliance with the Internationale. Disapproving of the approval of dual KMT and CSP membership as allowing external control over the party, Dai went into de facto exile during the reorganisation era, and Sun's death destroyed any restraint he had against the left and pushed him into a nearly suicidal pessimism.

As the Northern Expedition collapsed, the battered remnants of the National Revolutionary Army fighting in Fujian and Jiangxi who refused to join the rightist forces in the Long March decided to go underground and fight a protracted guerrilla war against the Zhili. These forces staged the large-scale but unsuccessful 1932 Shanghai Uprising against the increasing tyranny of the League of Eight Provinces, but were brutally quashed.

Undeterred, Song Qingling (widow of Sun Yat-sen), Li Jishen, Tan Pingshan, and Deng Yanda published the "Declaration to the Revolutionary People in China and the World" and announced the formation of the Provisional Action Committee of the Kuomintang to autonomously coordinate activities of the guerrilla remnants, now centred around the Fujian-Jiangxi Area (MinGan).

Most of their leaders were prominent in Guangdong politics and played leading roles in the original Whampoa Military Academy. Sympathisers, the Civil Engineering Clique, or the leftist wing of the Third Army, have sought to broker negotiations with these agrarian revolutionaries. But not everyone is so sure, as the PAC are very prone to stubbornness and are likely to be a thorn in the side of any who are not as dedicated to a socialist revolution as they are. / As the Northern Expedition collapsed, the battered remnants of the National Revolutionary Army fighting in Fujian and Jiangxi who refused to join the rightist forces in the Long March decided to go underground and fight a protracted guerrilla war against the Zhili. paths.name: The League of Chinese Syndicalists Collapses — Maybe we can have anarchism...in 3000 years.
paths.shortName: Maybe we can have anarchism...in 3000 years.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

The League of Chinese Syndicalists (LCS) was founded primarily by the Chinese Syndicalist Party (CSP) as a means of countering Kuomintang influence and expanding the limits of the United Front. The League almost immediately proved to be an unwieldy force as Marxists, Syndicalists, Anarchists, and various other independent leftists fought one another for influence. The rivals to the CSP, themselves divided into wings, are the anarchist (New) World Society led by the Four Elders of the Kuomintang.

The CSP, and the LCS by extension, is the raison d'etre of the right Kuomintang, which formed in opposition to the United Front. The right believes that China's unique socio-economic circumstances means class warfare and the dictatorship of the proletariat are unnecessary. While they reject the influence of the free market and note the social defects of the wage system, the right Kuomintang believe that Chinese capitalism is rudimentary enough that there is not yet a capitalist class consciousness.

Believing most stringently in the application of the Three Principles as opposed to any form of Marxism or Anarchism, Zhu Peide has nonetheless tentatively tabled discussion of incorporating the Chinese Syndicalists into the National Revolution.

One of the first members of the CSP, Wang Fusheng has been placed in a superior position within the party due to recent events, having been able to establish a provincial committee on behalf of the CSP's leadership. Operating with individuals such as Li Xin, the duo have entrenched themselves within the local student and worker movements.

Rather curiously, across the aisle, the Four Elders and their World Society have been viewed as far more palatable. Li Shizeng for example has called Marxist syndicalism regressive and Minsheng more compatible with the contemporary advances in human civilisation. The Kuomintang must lead a new third way against capitalism and syndicalism, two sides of western imperialism. To reconcile with the Four Elders would perhaps make it easier to keep the CSP in check. / The League of Chinese Syndicalists (LCS) was founded primarily by the Chinese Syndicalist Party (CSP) as a means of countering Kuomintang influence and expanding the limits of the United Front. Hu Zongnan's relationship with the members of the country is as idiosyncratic as it is diverse. One of General Chiang's many Zhejiang-born protégés, and recently transitioning into an extremist left-wing turn whilst in exile, he has amassed a significant group of radical Whampoa clique followers known as the China Revival Society, a secret society inspired by European totalist movements. The Director of the Training Department while abroad in exile, Hu's influence has inoculated party extremism in a generation of leftist cadets.

With their only, ironic, brothers in arms in the Blue Shirts Society having been diminished significantly in influence, very few within the Party at present have the capacity to stomach ingratiating with a plethora of syndicalist-spouting extremists. Albeit, rather curiously, the Civil Engineering Clique have pressed The Leader to accept some of the CRS' membership, at least on principle grounds. With Whampoa seemingly aiding Whampoa, it is evidently clear that the CEC intend to harness the CRS' zealotry for their own needs.

However, besides opposition from the majority of the party, even the CRS' own fellow leftists (beyond the CEC) have denounced them as being counterrevolutionary, Even worse, Old Right and New Right members of the party have decried them as socialist infiltrators, whilst the various civilians of the party decry them as being too extreme. / He Yingqin never got along that well with Hu Zongnan, one of General Chiang's many Zhejiang-born protégés, and that was before his radical turn while in exile. Hu has amassed a diverse group of extremist Whampoa clique followers known as the China Revival Society, a secret society inspired by European totalist movements. The Director of the Training Department while abroad in exile, Hu's influence has inoculated party extremism in a generation of leftist cadets.

Ironically, or according to some not surprisingly, they have found ready sympathisers in the Blue Shirts Society. Teng Jie and his allies share an ultra-nationalistic instinct, and believe that with the right encouragement Generals Hu Zongnan, Deng Wenyi, and He Zhonghan will be willing to drop the syndicalist nonsense in their platform in favour of a patriotic form of revolution. Teng has asked Liu Jianqun, He's personal secretary and confidant to intercede on their behalf. Liu has argued that unlike the other socialists and liberals in the left, the CRS adhere to a purer, true socialism more akin to Dr. Sun's vision rather than the corrupted form found in the degenerate west.

Besides He Yingqin, there are plenty of others who are wary of the CRS. Most of their fellow leftists have denounced them as being counterrevolutionary, the far right accuse them of being socialist infiltrators, and the civilian wings of the party decry them as being too extreme.

With both He Yingqin and Dai Jitao (at least temporarily) out of the picture, Minister of War Zhang Qun's appointment to the Presidency was quickly confirmed by the panicked members of the Central Executive Committee. The President-elect has turned out to be far more free-thinking than most gave him credit for however, and his first move in office has been to nominate Yang Yongtai as Premier of the Executive Yuan instead of Chen Guofu.

The stunned Central Executive Committee, which has spent the past few years effectively rubber stamping the will of the President, has awkwardly approved the appointment. The Zhang-Yang government has moved quickly to appoint sympathetic ministers from the Political Science Clique's braintrust to the cabinet, trying to sideline their rivals in the CC Clique. Similarly, Zhang Qun has assembled a small clique of aligned officers in the National Revolutionary Army, including Generals Li Genyuan, Lai Shihuang, and Xiong Shihui with orders to keep the army under control.

Zhang, in his hurried array of public addresses and speeches before the National Assembly, has attempted to consolidate his position. He has stressed the need for unity and negotiation with the South China Political Council and also reiterated the Political Science Clique's desire to pass the provisional constitution. How he intends to reconcile the two objectives he has not said, and given how much of a sticking point the matter has been it is unlikely to be easy. Perhaps he is gambling that the fear of He Yingqin's return (and his revenge) will motivate party moderates to action, but if that is the case he is making a very dangerous wager.
objectives: When “Zhang Qun's Audacious Gambit” becomes available, choose “The Political Science Clique makes yet another bid for power.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Hu Ruoyu Marches on Kunming — Yunnan returns to reaction.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Hu Ruoyu Marches on Kunming” becomes available, choose “Yunnan returns to reaction.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The revolutionaries in the Kuomintang have evidently worn out their welcome in Yunnan as Hu Ruoyu's forces surged from Mengzi to Kunming with little resistance. The overstretched Third Army garrisons were rapidly overrun, a process accelerated by an uprising in the city organised by General Lu Han, a staff officer under Long Yun, who avenged his relative and avoided the need for a long siege.

The vaunted Whampoa Spirit proved to be little more than talk as Chen Cheng's forces were destroyed assaulting Old Dian Clique positions. After regrouping their forces, Hu Ruoyu and Lu Han were able to capture Guizhou after routing their opponents. While the two nominally retain their Kuomintang membership and profess their absolute loyalty to the revolution, the party's true faithful have been driven out of the Southwest.

The ensuing political situation has been tense. While the central government has been too preoccupied to be concerned with Southwestern Affairs and have refrained from commenting on the situation, ironically the lack of an external threat has destabilised the province. Tang Jiyao is an absolute persona non-grata to the KMT, but Long Yun's is more divisive. The Kunming garrison and provincial elders briefly installed him as Governor, but clashes between him and his long-time rival Hu Ruoyu (who now has the upper hand) caused them to trade accusations of counterrevolutionary behavior.

Long hoped to shore up his failing position by counting on the support of Lu Han, whose forces are slowly trickling back from Guizhou. But General Lu decided to make a fateful decision - coming to an agreement with Hu Ruoyu behind his back and agreeing to accept Hu as Governor to avoid further conflict. Long Yun, invited to participate in the planned junta, has left Kunming for Zhaotong - unwilling to be a figurehead and hoping for more favorable winds in the future.
objectives: When “Hu Ruoyu Marches on Kunming” becomes available, choose “Yunnan returns to reaction.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Hu Ruoyu Seizes Kunming — Hu's finally had his revenge.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Hu Ruoyu Seizes Kunming” becomes available, choose “Hu's finally had his revenge.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The coup was swift, faster than anyone could have imagined. Tang Jiyao's rule proved far more fragile than it seemed - his advanced forces melting away as the Mengzi Army advanced. Zhang Ruiji led the left flank and quickly captured Dali as local gentry militias joined him along the way. Hu Ruoyu and Li Xuanting meanwhile made a rapid march to the capital.

Kunming fell almost without a shot, preventing the need for a long siege. Tang Jiyao's attempt to convince the assembly to denounce the Mengzi Clique fell short as conservatives in the Provincial Assembly and the Chamber of Commerce broke ranks as news of early battlefield defeats spread. Soon retreat became a route as Hu's army reached the gates of the city - amid CDL led protests in the city, General Long Yun staged a palace coup and detained Governor Tang, installing himself as acting Governor.

A restoration attempt by Tang Jiyao's loyalists in the north was quickly quashed. As word of the coup reached Guizhou, the Liu clan arrested Tang Jiyu before he could return to Yunnan. Tang's other loyalists like Tang Jilin, Wang Jiexiu, and Wu Xuexian are simply too scattered and demoralised to resist for long.

The plotters in Kunming have sent representatives to negotiate to the victorious Mengzi triumvirate, but General Hu has demanded nothing short of a surrender. Realising their precarious situation, Long's own generals - led by his kinsman Lu Han - betrayed him rather than fight. Unwilling to participate in the coming junta as a powerless figurehead, Long has decided to "sweep his family's tombs" in Zhaotong, hoping for a better opportunity. In his place, General Lu Han has sought to capitalise on CDL discontent. But for now, Hu Ruoyu is the master of the southwest and has been promptly recognised as Governor by the central government.
objectives: When “Hu Ruoyu Seizes Kunming” becomes available, choose “Hu's finally had his revenge.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Opposition Putsch in Kunming — Tang Jiyao's supporters will be removed from their posts!
paths.shortName: Tang Jiyao's supporters will be removed from their posts!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “Opposition Putsch in Kunming” becomes available, choose “Tang Jiyao's supporters will be removed from their posts!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

The coup was swift, faster than anyone could have imagined. Tang Jiyao's rule proved far more fragile than it seemed, with the provincial assembly and chamber of commerce rebelling as he attempted to secure their support for martial law. The CDL turned out thousands of protesters in the streets and with the Governor's legitimacy dropping fast the sidelined General Long Yun was able to muster the support needed for a palace coup.

In the countryside, guerrillas and bandits loosely aligned with the CDL were able to seize control of several towns as the decapitated Tang forces began to melt away. A restoration attempt by Tang Jiyao's loyalists in the north was quickly quashed. As word of the coup reached Guizhou, the Liu clan arrested Tang Jiyu before he could return to Yunnan. Tang's other loyalists like Tang Jilin, Wang Jiexiu, and Wu Xuexian are simply too scattered and demoralised to resist for long. With the armed wing of Tang's movement destroyed, most of the fragile PGP's members have either deserted the party or fled to Guangzhou to avoid retribution.

Hu Ruoyu's forces proved slow to leave Mengzi, delayed by various internal disputes and sabotage by rural forces. With his window to Kunming closing, he has decided to accept an agreement with Cun Shusheng, Long Yun, Miao Yuntai, and Zhang Taiyan to form a provisional council. As Cun Shusheng, the nominal head of the council, works to explain the situation with the central government, the fate of Tang's loyalists hangs in the balance.

paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

Tang Jiyao's enemies were fast, but Tang was faster. He quickly mustered the support of the assembly to declare a state of emergency and gathered his guard divisions to secure Kunming. Scattered CDL and socialist protests in the city were quickly put down and wavering forces fell in line.

In Zhaotong and Dali, loyalists were able to hold off attempts to seize the major towns and cities by local bandits, guerrillas, and gentry militias. Fortifying their positions, they were able to secure Tang's western flank before the Mengzi Army's vanguard could link up with sympathetic forces.

Hu Ruoyu's main forces took far too long to leave Mengzi, suffering from low morale and poor organisation. When they finally met Tang's army, it was too late - Kunming units were dug in and ready for a fight. General Hu's forces were easily beaten back and Tang's forces gave chase all the way to Mengzi where the triumvirate were forced to capitulate. Their plots unravelled by the wily Governor, the rebels plead for mercy at his feet.

paths.name: The Federal Government Orders Tang to Stand Down — We will have our revenge against the tyrants!
paths.shortName: We will have our revenge against the tyrants!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Federal Government Orders Tang to Stand Down” becomes available, choose “We will have our revenge against the tyrants!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Cun Shusheng's persuasive petition to the President must have worked! Word has quickly spread that The Leader has publicly ordered Governor Tang to cease his crackdown at once and peacefully resolve the crisis engulfing his province, with unspecified consequences should he refuse. This wades into some questionable constitutional territory, as the Federalist Movement traditionally has espoused the need for the central government to avoid meddling in local affairs, though some have argued there ought to be exceptions for enforcing free elections, civil rights, and/or protecting national sovereignty.

Tang Jiyao never got the chance to respond however. Tang's waning popularity and plummeting authority has exposed his weakness, and within a day a group of his generals led by a vengeful Long Yun orchestrated a palace coup - detaining Tang and many of his key loyalists in a decapitation strike. Seeking to legitimise the putsch, he has agreed to a provisional council including Cun, Long, Zhang Taiyan, and Hu Ruoyu - who has reluctantly agreed to terms. Tang Jiyao remains officially governor for now, but he has been rendered effectively a figurehead.

A restoration attempt by Tang Jiyao's loyalists in the north was quickly quashed. As word of the coup reached Guizhou, the Liu clan arrested Tang Jiyu before he could return to Yunnan. Tang's other loyalists like Tang Jilin, Wang Jiexiu, and Wu Xuexian are simply too scattered and demoralised to resist for long. Many of his followers, fearing retribution, have fled to neighbouring provinces as the balance of power has shifted - no doubt coming up with slander against us.

The central government is not likely to be particularly happy about the outcome, but they are also likely to be eager to wash their hands of the situation, at least for now. A precedent has been irrevocably set now, which may lead to thorny issues down the line.

paths.name: The Federal Government Reaffirms Tang's Authority — Tang will have his revenge against traitors.
paths.shortName: Tang will have his revenge against traitors.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
When “The Federal Government Reaffirms Tang's Authority” becomes available, choose “Tang will have his revenge against traitors.”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

Cun Shusheng and the CDL's attempts to enlist the support of the President against Governor Tang has backfired. Rather than come to their rescue, The Leader has written a public response chastising the CDL for undermining Tang's authority and trying to incite violence, repeating the provincial government's claims that the CDL are in league with socialist revolutionaries and opportunistic bandits. Furthermore, it cited past agreements within the Federalist movement protecting the provinces from undue central government interference in local affairs, and tasked Tang to resolve his differences amicably with his detractors.

Of course, this was all that Tang needed to reassert control over the province. With the central government seemingly behind him, wavering officers in his government fell in line and Kunming was quickly able to complete its crackdown against suspected traitors inside the city. The CDL, having lost its initiative by waiting for a central government response, proved powerless as their opportunity slipped by.

Hu Ruoyu's grand march on Kunming similarly never materialised - his gamble that regional powerholders would rally to his side amid Tang Jiyao's weakness failed. Most Yunnan Clique forces remained loyal to Tang and the Mengzi faction's undisciplined forces melted away after a failed assault on loyalist positions. His dominance now assured, there is little left standing in Tang's way now.

Most curious to many within the New Right is that of Chen Cheng's actual leanings within the Party. Some allude that his ties to his mentor Deng Yanda never truly died, that he is but a mere secret member of the Provisional Action Committee, seeing as he is a blood brother of Zhou Zhirou. Others claim that he is merely the orthodox successor to Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, implementing the "Red General's" policies to the utmost. Truthfully, whilst those close to him may claim he has socialist sympathies, Generalissimo Chen is thoroughly a member of the growing New Right.

Coinciding with this, Generalissimo Chen recently instituted a cadre system to enforce the party's influence amongst membership. With each cadre provided thorough training on Sun's Three Principles, and tested for loyalty to the Party and their capability, Party work has also received a change of direction. Targetting both the Party membership and general society, Chen hopes that popular sentiment towards the KMT can be cultivated, and that investigations into local situations can provide information, and root out illegal activity.

Furthermore, party recruitment has been transformed to accommodate for more of the lower classes, the farmers, workers and intellectuals have all been prioritised. Whilst they will most likely not participate in education, propaganda, public service or other Party Work, it has been deemed a stride towards equalisation of the peasantry with the masses by the remnant Provisional Action Committee within the nation.

Such good rapport and acclamation by the PAC's Deng Yanda has seen the leftist organisation offer a sort of olive branch towards the Little Generalissimo. Following with recent exchanges with other leftists such as Zhou Enlai, Deng has offered the PAC's assistance in enlightening the peasantry, in exchange for amnesties and a continued prioritisation of the Chinese lower classes.

United once more as Student and Teacher, the vanguard duo of the legendary Li Genyuan and stalwart Zhu Peide managed to successfully weather all storms that crashed against their walls. Navigating opposition from radicals on the left and right, the Kuomintang regime would aid in the ever relentless stride of the National Revolution. And in the Party's darkest moment, Li and Zhu would march forward like their beloved Cai E had done decades before.

Despite their triumphs it has become swiftly apparent that the Li-Zhu alliance is coming to its conclusion. With his ambitions difficult to sate, and having re-entered the spotlight with the backing of his old allies in the well-funded Political Science Clique, Li Genyuan has utilised the clique's full political machine to stake his own claim for party leadership of the Kuomintang.

For his part Zhu Peide has been rumoured to be in talks with better established factions within the party, dangling a potential Premiership to entice them to his side. Evidently, Zhu aims to push Li from power and install a more amenable candidate. Amongst his suitors are the three major titans of the old right: Sun Fo and his Reconstruction Faction, Zou Lu and Western Hills, and even that of Hu Hanmin and the Elders Clique. Enticed by a return to power, they are also suspicious of Li Genyuan and the PSC with their deviation from party orthodoxy.

Under immense pressure, Zhu has been forced into calling for an election for Chairmanship of the Party, and with it the Presidency of the Republic. Having lost his main pillar of support, Zhu has been forced to scramble for allies and a major agreement with the Old Right would grant him enough votes to consolidate support. On the flipside, Li has begun to parley with his old close friend Gu Zhongxiu, a traditional North KMT-Beiyang candidate. However, Zhang Qun has made his move pressing the young guard of the PSC to sponsor Yang Yongtai as his Premier.
objectives: When “The Party Election” becomes available, choose “Li Genyuan claims his title, and appoints Gu Zhongxiu!”. This may be a later election or an alternative within a broader political route.

paths.name: Democracy's Martyrs — Chen Jiongming / Ye Ju / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Liu Wenhui has won, but at a terrible cost.
paths.shortName: Chen Jiongming / Ye Ju / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Liu Wenhui has won, but at a terrible cost.
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested

The protests got off to a slow start, but began to grow as the CDL worked to rally their followers to oppose Chen Jiongming / Ye Ju / Tang Xiaoying / Tang Jiyao / Liu Wenhui's power play. The Yunnan Army struck hard and struck fast - crippling the budding opposition. Army cadets have organised throngs of loyalists to assault CDL protesters while the police raided the homes of their leaders.

Even more chilling were the assassinations in broad daylight. Li Furen and Wang Ren were shot in Xi'an. Li Gongpu, one of the "Seven Gentlemen" and a prominent NSF organiser, suffered a severe head injury at the hands of a pro-government mob. Recuperating in Kunming, he was shot and stabbed by officers from the local garrison while taking a walk.

An enraged Wen Yiduo gave an impromptu speech at Li's funeral three days later, delivering scathing remarks at the heart of the Dian Clique's power. He defiantly addressed the secret agents embedded in the crowd, declaring that "we are not afraid of death. We are ready to follow in Li's footsteps! The moment we step out the door, we do not think of stepping back in." Later that afternoon, he was riddled by gunfire while leaving his office building.

His martyrdom has triggered an outpouring of grief. In many of Wen's poems, he had described his hope for a "death in ecstasy", dying in perfect beauty in the pursuit of one's ideals. A heroic act of sacrifice and fulfillment. The charismatic teacher and a politician once dramatically stretched out his hands to an audience holding chalk powder, insisting that as scholars the CDL have no blood on their hands. He asked the crowd not to belittle his pure, clean hands for they can "change history and create miracles."

The backlash has been great, but it is too late for the Dian Clique to back down now. CDL leaders continue to be hunted down and assaulted. Another, Sun Zhongyuan, was killed in Beijing while Dao Xingzhi died of a stroke in Shanghai. Curfews have been imposed, publications shuttered, and many have fled the country.

Long Yun has come a long way in such a short period of time. Once a subordinate officer for an outlying warlord, he became Governor and then a pretender and now suddenly he has become the undisputed President of all of China. But this newfound power comes with weighty responsibilities and he cannot rule alone.

Building the government needed to see China's post-war reconstruction starts with appointing a sympathetic Prime Minister to head the government. paths.name: Lu Han's Uprising — Lu Han was in control of the capital!
paths.shortName: Lu Han was in control of the capital!
paths.sourceStatus: Source-defined political outcome; availability not playtested
paths.notes:
